finding: FR3-1: tool_call_lookup_indexes_are_owner_leading advertises 'every index covering a column list_calls_for_user filters', but FILTERED hardcodes 2 of the 5 filtered columns — the assertion is narrower than its own docstring.

finding: FR3-2: the migration replay only matched statements starting with 'CREATE INDEX', so the canonical violation written as 'CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... (tool_use_id)' was silently ignored and the guard stayed green.

finding: FR3-6: resolveStep returned the CONTRIBUTION's key, discarding segmentRail's `${key}#${i}` disambiguation for a repeated tool_use_id. finding: FR3-7: the sole caller discarded resolveElicitationVia's boolean, documented as existing 'so a caller can surface not-resolvable rather than silently claiming success'. With no transport installed a click on Approve/Deny flipped a spinner and did nothing — no message, no error, no state change. A behavioural regression versus the direct McpComposer call AP-4 replaced, which POSTed regardless of extension init.

finding: FR3-8: when the decision lands the Approve/Deny buttons are UNMOUNTED and replaced by plain text with no live region, so the element holding keyboard focus is destroyed and a screen reader is told nothing.

finding: FR3-9: setElicitationTransport called provider.subscribe outside any try/catch — the one write path in a module whose read paths are all guarded. A throwing subscribe left an INSTALLED transport with no change subscription (every card frozen at the status it first read) and escaped into the registering extension's initialize, which the registry only logs.
fix: Refuses the install and clears the slot, honouring the file's own degrade-cleanly contract. Pinned by transport.test.ts.

finding: FR3-10: resolveElicitationVia awaited provider.resolve with no catch. Safe only because today's provider swallows internally; the published contract promises optimistic-update-plus-rollback, not non-rejection, so a second provider that rejects floats an unhandled rejection out of an onClick — a gating HIGH page-error under gallery:runtime.
fix: Wrapped; a rejecting provider is reported as unresolved (false) and surfaced by the card.

finding: FR3-11: registerElicitation swallowed every failure with a bare comment-only catch and returned void. The consumer injects its card unconditionally after the call, so a dropped registration left a card pending forever with zero diagnostic anywhere.
fix: Returns boolean and logs; all three swallow paths now emit console.error.

finding: FR3-12: the transport's subscribe forwarded the ENTIRE mcp store, so every addToolCall/updateToolCall/setToolCallProgress/server-selection mutation re-rendered every mounted approval card. A strict widening over the code it replaced, which read elicitationRequests through the store proxy's per-property useShallow selector.
fix: Notifies only when the elicitationRequests Map identity changes. Verified sound: the store is immer + enableMapSet, so every elicitation mutation replaces the Map.

finding: FR3-13: the AP-4 move relocated the formatter into core but kept the EXTENSION's name in the core API (mcpServerParenLabel) — core naming an extension, the thing the rail's own INV-1 guard exists to prevent one directory over.
fix: Renamed to serverParenLabel; all five call sites repointed. The function has zero mcp domain knowledge.

finding: FR3-14: hasElicitationTransport and __resetElicitationTransportForTests had ZERO callers, and the 192-line core seam shipped with no test file at all — so owner-scoped teardown, re-registration detach, degrade-when-absent and every catch branch were unreachable from any test. Its precedent liveSteps.ts is unit-tested through exactly this reset helper.
fix: transport.test.ts (7 tests) exercises all of it; hasElicitationTransport is now consumed by JsToolApprovalContent to pre-empt a dead Approve/Deny.

finding: FR3-15: the steps-collapsed assertion sat OUTSIDE the aria-expanded branch. A rail that INV-4/INV-5 FORCE OPEN renders its summary as a plain div with no aria-expanded and no collapse control, so no click happened, the steps stayed rendered, and this INV-3 acceptance spec would go RED on a design-conformant rendering of INV-4/INV-5.
fix: The collapse assertion moved inside the toggleable branch; the forced-open case asserts what INV-3 actually governs there (the breakout survives).

finding: FR3-16: non-falsifiable clauses — a getByRole('button', {name: /^(collapse|hide)/}) probe matching nothing the kit renders; a full-width check that merely restated the w-full class the same commit added; a page-scoped mcp-tool-approval-card assertion where the claim was 'inside the breakout'; an opacity read on the button only (CSS opacity composites down the ancestor chain); and rail selection via .first(), which could pick the quiet-single shape that renders no summary and silently no-op the whole block.
fix: Vacuous probe removed rather than left reading as coverage; width compared against a real rail row; card assertion scoped to the breakout; effective opacity walked up the ancestor chain; the rail filtered to one that HAS a summary.

finding: FR3-17: the disclosure loop cached the count before the first click (so a disclosure revealed by expanding an earlier one was never actuated) and used click({force:true}), which bypasses actionability — a genuinely obscured or zero-size control still counted as actuated.
fix: Re-reads the set each iteration and clicks without force, with a bound so it cannot loop unbounded.

finding: FR3-18: idx_mcp_tool_calls_server and idx_mcp_tool_calls_conv are single-column, so the same user_id-as-post-Filter shape 202607200200 argues against still occurs on the ?server_id= / ?conversation_id= probes.
disposition: PRE-EXISTING (202607140180), not created by this branch. Fixing means a new migration rewriting indexes this feature never touched — scope growth, not scope completion. Named explicitly in the guard's LEGACY_SINGLE_COLUMN allowlist so it is recorded rather than hidden, and any NEW index on those columns is now forced owner-leading.

finding: FR3-19: this file's prose is stale once 202607200200 drops its two indexes, and carries no forward pointer.
disposition: CANNOT be fixed in place. sqlx stores a checksum per applied migration and Migrator::run fails with VersionMismatch when a file's bytes change after it was applied; core/database/mod.rs sets only set_ignore_missing(true), which does not relax the checksum. Editing the prose would hard-fail boot for every developer who has already booted this branch — which is precisely why 202607200200 exists as a second file. The forward pointer lives in 202607200200's own header instead.

finding: FR3-20: the composite indexes only serve the query under a CUSTOM plan; a deployment pinning plan_cache_mode=force_generic_plan degrades to a bitmap scan no index shape rescues.
disposition: Measured, documented and deliberate in FIX_ROUND-2 with EXPLAIN evidence: the generic plan costs 4184.81 against 8.46-755.23 for every custom shape, so plan_cache_mode=auto never switches (verified behaviourally over 8 executions). Restructuring the query would rewrite the cross-user guard TEST-17 pins, to buy a plan PostgreSQL's own cost model rejects by up to 495x.

finding: FR3-21: registration happens in initialize (per pane mount) while the owner-scoped clear runs from unregister, whose only caller is register()'s HMR re-registration path — so after an HMR re-register the transport stays null until a pane remounts.
disposition: PRE-EXISTING shape shared with the rail live source (setRailLiveSource / clearRailLiveSourceIfOwnedBy), which this seam deliberately mirrors. Dev-HMR-only; changing the lifecycle contract for one of the two seams would desynchronise them. Belongs in a single change that moves BOTH.

finding: FR3-22: transport.ts is a near-verbatim structural clone of liveSteps.ts (singleton + owner + unsubscribe + version + listeners + bump + set/clearIfOwnedBy + subscribe + __reset); a third seam would copy it again. A shared createOwnedSeam<T>() factory would remove ~60 duplicated lines.
disposition: A genuine refactor candidate, not a defect: both copies are correct and now both are unit-tested. Extracting the factory touches the rail live source, which is load-bearing for INV-4/INV-9 and outside this fix round's blast radius. Recorded for the next round rather than folded in silently.

finding: FR3-23: ExternalMcpMockServer.start() throws on a loopback-only host (nonLoopbackIpv4) and binds 0.0.0.0, which prompts the macOS/Windows firewall; the spec's only guard is the bridge skip, so such a host reports FAIL rather than SKIP.
disposition: Inherited verbatim from the pre-existing consumer (07-mcp/external-approval-full-disclosure.spec.ts), which documents the same limitation. Adding a capability skip belongs in the SHARED fixture, and B3 forbids editing shared test infrastructure to route around this feature's problem. Recorded against the fixture, not patched locally.

finding: FR3-24: the ['modules/mcp','modules/js-tool'] half of the AP-4 pair is an idle control — nothing under modules/mcp has ever imported js-tool, so that direction cannot go red for the change under audit.
disposition: Working as designed. AP-4's whole failure mode was the coupling INVERTING rather than disappearing (mcp->js-tool became js-tool->mcp); a guard that pinned only the direction that happens to be live today would not catch it inverting back. The js-tool->mcp direction carries the negative control and is verified red-on-violation; the reverse is the symmetry that makes the pair meaningful.

finding: FR3-25: data-step-key on the breakout has no production reader — its only consumer is the new e2e spec.
disposition: Not dead code: it is test-affordance markup of the same class as the data-testid attributes the whole kit ships and the testid registry gates. It is what makes INV-3 falsifiable against a model-chosen identity on a real stream, and FR3-6 fixed the namespace bug that would otherwise have made that assertion vacuous.

finding: FR4-1: the FIX_ROUND-3 widening of FILTERED was wrong in BOTH directions — it added workflow_run_id, which list_calls_for_user never filters on (INSERT-only), and dropped is_built_in, which it does ($4::bool IS NULL OR is_built_in = $4). The fictional entry then forced a third LEGACY_SINGLE_COLUMN exemption, hiding the real gap: a single-column index on is_built_in still slipped through.
fix: FILTERED read off the query, not the table: {server_id, conversation_id, is_built_in, tool_use_id, message_id}. Allowlist back to 2 entries and PINNED TO THE EXACT COLUMN VECTOR, so a future migration re-creating the same NAME over a different column set is not silently exempt. Negative control run: a single-column index on is_built_in now turns the guard RED.

finding: FR4-2: the FIX_ROUND-3 walk stopped at src/modules/*, but compose_merged_migrations unions five named SDK crate dirs and desktop/tauri — 101 of 109 applied files seen, so an index authored from an SDK migration still escaped.
fix: Walks the same union build.rs composes; the vacuity assert raised from >50 to >100 files.

finding: FR4-3: valid SQL still slipping past the replay parser — (1) the recogniser tested the uppercased form but extracted the name from the case-SENSITIVE original, so a lowercase `create index` was recorded under the name 'create'; (2) CONCURRENTLY was trimmed on CREATE but not DROP, so `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY x` failed to remove the index (false RED); (3) ALTER TABLE ... ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE creates a real backing index and was invisible; (4) block comments were not stripped, so commented-out DDL registered as real.
fix: Name extraction maps the uppercased head back onto the original spelling; CONCURRENTLY trimmed on both paths; an ALTER TABLE ... UNIQUE on mcp_tool_calls now PANICS with a directive rather than being silently ignored; /* */ stripped before parsing. Three negative controls run: lowercase DDL -> RED, is_built_in single-column -> RED, block-commented DDL -> correctly ignored.

finding: FR4-4: registerElicitation's new boolean was still discarded at its ONLY call site, and the card was still injected unconditionally — i.e. the exact 'card pending forever, silently' case the return value was introduced to expose remained live whenever a healthy transport's register throws.
fix: The outcome is carried onto the card as `unresolvable`, so the injected card states it cannot be answered instead of offering live buttons over an entry the provider does not have.

finding: FR4-5: the FIX_ROUND-3 banner said the request cannot be answered while Approve/Deny stayed mounted, enabled and clickable — contradicting the docstring the same round wrote ('Consumed by JsToolApprovalContent to DISABLE + explain'). Clicking still spun and did nothing.
fix: Both controls take disabled={unresolvable}, and resolve() early-returns on it. Contract and code now agree.

finding: FR4-6: both role=status regions were MOUNTED together with their text. A live region that enters the accessibility tree already carrying its content is announced unreliably by NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver — the region must pre-exist and its contents change. The FIX_ROUND-3 comment claimed the opposite, so the code read as covered when it was not. Focus was still dropped to <body> when the buttons unmount.
fix: ONE always-mounted role=status region whose CONTENTS change, tabIndex={-1}, focused on the pending->resolved transition so focus is restored and the outcome is announced.

finding: FR4-7: `unresolvable` was latched in state and only cleared at the start of the next resolve(), so a transport installed after a failed attempt left the red banner up with no way to clear it.
fix: Derived, not latched: `data.unresolvable || resolveFailed || !hasElicitationTransport()`, re-read on every seam bump, so it clears itself the moment mcp installs a transport.

finding: FR4-8: FIX_ROUND-3 hardened transport.ts and left its explicitly-cited twin untouched. setRailLiveSource is registered from the SAME mcp initialize two statements earlier and still had a bare unsubscribe and a bare subscribe — so the identical failure (a live source installed with no change subscription, every rail step frozen, and the throw aborting the rest of mcp's wiring INCLUDING the elicitation transport) was live.
fix: Same refuse-the-install + guarded-unsubscribe treatment. The two seams are hardened identically, as their shared docstring already claimed.

finding: FR4-9: FIX_ROUND-3 narrowed the elicitation subscribe with an explicit rationale and left the IDENTICAL whole-store widening 25 lines above on setRailLiveSource — where it costs more: every mcp mutation bumped railLiveVersion, re-rendering every mounted ActivityRail, each re-running resolveStep over every step through the whole contribution registry.
fix: Narrowed to toolCalls Map identity. Verified sound: addToolCall/updateToolCall/setToolCallProgress all write through state.toolCalls.set(...) under immer + enableMapSet, so identity changes on every relevant mutation and nothing else.

finding: FR4-10: the width probe FIX_ROUND-3 added to replace a tautology reintroduced the defect class it was closing — a document-wide querySelector('[data-testid="rail-step"]') that can match another message's row, and that goes falsely RED against the QUIET-SINGLE rail shape, whose row renders at full bubble width by design (DEC-3).
fix: Scoped to an INDENTED rail ([data-rail-shape="rail"]) inside the SAME bubble — the only shape for which 'not laid out as a rail row' is a claim at all.

finding: FR4-11: the isSibling probe was left on the UNFILTERED first rail while the locator two lines above was narrowed, so the branch could be entered on rail A and assert siblinghood of rail B.
fix: Evaluated on the same narrowed rail locator.

finding: FR4-12: the most behaviour-affecting UI fix of FIX_ROUND-3 (preserving segmentation's key across re-resolution) shipped with no test — the one-line revert `return resolved` turned nothing red.
fix: Extracted as the pure exported helper withSegmentationKey (segmentation owns identity, re-resolution owns state) and pinned by two railSegmentation tests. Negative control run: reverting the helper body turns the suite RED ('segmentation owns the identity'), green on restore.

finding: FR4-13: the FIX_ROUND-3 comment claimed the disambiguation also protects the detail-panel tab id. It does not — toolCallTabId derives from step.toolUseId, never from step.key.
fix: Comment corrected, and the correction states plainly that same-tool_use_id steps share a right-panel tab both before and after the fix.

finding: FR4-14: FIX_ROUND-3 turned the previously-silent no-transport no-ops into console.error, which scripts/runtime-health.mjs classifies as a HIGH GATING finding — so the gallery state that exists to SHOW the degraded approval card would have failed gate:ui.
fix: The documented degraded state (no transport installed) logs at warn; a provider that THROWS stays at error. The diagnostic is kept without gating the gallery on a designed state.

finding: FR4-15: __resetElicitationTransportForTests called unsubscribe unguarded while the production path in the same file now wraps it, so a throwing unsubscribe would abort the reset with transport still set and leak it into the next spec.
fix: Guarded; the reset always completes.

finding: FR4-16: two holes left in the widened importsOf — `foo();import 'x'` (valid JS, not line-anchored) evaded both guards, and because importsOf does not strip comments a documentation example of the forbidden import would be a FALSE POSITIVE.
fix: Comments stripped first; the anchor widened to (?:^|[;}\s])import. Four controls run: bare side-effect, mid-line no-space, barrel `@/modules/mcp` -> all RED; a block-commented example -> correctly green.

finding: FR4-17: moving the steps-collapsed assertion inside the aria-expanded branch removed the false RED but leaves block 5's stated 'collapsing the rail does not hide the request' claim unexercised in this spec — at the pending-approval moment the turn is still streaming, so the rail is force-open and non-toggleable.
disposition: Correct as designed, and now SAID so in the spec rather than implied. A real stream cannot guarantee a settled toggleable rail at the approval moment; the deterministic collapse proof is owned by the mocked sibling spec (activity-rail-breakout.spec.ts), which can. Forcing it here would mean either a flaky assertion or mocking the stream — the exact thing this spec exists to avoid.

finding: FR4-18: the fix pins `key` from segmentation but `consumed` and `blocking` still come from re-resolution, so a tool entering pending-approval after segmentation re-resolves to blocking:true while still rendering as a rail row.
disposition: By design, and load-bearing. ITEM-5's whole point is that segmentation decides the SHAPE of a message exactly ONCE so the span/render desync is structurally impossible; shape is read from the segments array, never from a re-resolved descriptor. `key` is identity (segmentation's), which is why it is pinned; `consumed`/`blocking` are not consulted for shape after segmentation. Pinning them would not change any rendering and would blur the very separation the fix restores.

finding: FR4-19: dropping click({force:true}) means a genuinely un-actionable control hangs until the 300s test timeout rather than failing fast, because actionTimeout is unset.
disposition: The premise is wrong: playwright.config.ts sets `use.actionTimeout: 10000` globally, and this spec does not override it. An un-actionable disclosure fails in 10s with Playwright's actionability report — which is the whole reason force was dropped.

finding: FR5-1: the FIX_ROUND-4 focus effect STEALS FOCUS ON MOUNT. `wasResolved` was seeded null, so any mount where `resolved !== null` satisfied the guard and called focus(). The transcript is virtualized (@tanstack/react-virtual) and this card's resolved state is DESIGNED to survive a remount, so merely scrolling an answered approval back into view yanked focus out of the composer and scroll-jumped the viewport.
fix: The ref is seeded with the first-render value, so only a genuine null->resolved TRANSITION moves focus. Found independently by both round-5 auditors.

finding: FR5-2: FIX_ROUND-4 created a permanent dead-end AND a regression. `resolveFailed` fed `unresolvable`, which both disabled the buttons and gated resolve() — so the setResolveFailed(false) reset inside resolve() became unreachable and one failed POST disabled the card for the life of the mount. Before FIX_ROUND-4 the same failure left the buttons clickable and reset on retry.
fix: Replaced the collapsed boolean with elicitationBlockedReason() -> 'no-transport' | 'resolve-failed' | null. Only no-transport disables (nothing can carry the decision); resolve-failed stays RETRYABLE with its own message ('That didn't go through — try again'). Pinned by a unit test incl. the recovery case.

finding: FR5-3: FIX_ROUND-4 wrote `unresolvable: !registered` into the run_js_approval block's CONTENT — a transient client transport condition recorded in the message content vocabulary, snapshotted once and never correctable (the block is deduped by elicitation_id and never rewritten). Because mcp's initialize awaits a dynamic import BEFORE installing the transport, a frame landing in that window latched the card into a permanently disabled state even after mcp finished wiring.
fix: Removed from the block entirely. The card RECONCILES against the live seam and SELF-HEALS: once a transport exists and the entry is missing, it re-registers. The failure now repairs itself instead of being recorded as message content.

finding: FR5-4: withSegmentationKey pinned only `key`, but `key` is not the only SHAPE field segmentation owns. segmentRail CLAMPS `consumed` to the first RAIL_EXCLUDED block after the anchor — the ITEM-5 guard against a contribution swallowing the prose answer — and ActivityRail passes the RE-RESOLVED step to renderStepDetail, which reads placed.step.consumed. So an over-reporting contribution had its clamp bypassed at detail-render time and redrew blocks the segmentation loop already rendered.
fix: Renamed to withSegmentationShape and pins key + consumed + blocking. THIS REVERSES FR4-18, which I rejected on the reasoning that shape is never read from a re-resolved descriptor — that was wrong on the facts; renderStepDetail reads it. The auditor's file:line evidence beat my reasoning.

finding: FR5-5: the anti-vacuity guard `files.len() > 100` sits BELOW the 101 files the pre-FIX_ROUND-4 module-only walk already produced (101 modules + 8 SDK + 5 desktop = 114). Dropping the SDK roots leaves 101 and dropping desktop leaves 109 — both still pass. The guard could not detect either regression it was raised for.
fix: Asserts PER ROOT that each group contributed files, so losing any root fails immediately.

finding: FR5-6: EVERY FIX_ROUND-4 parser change is inert on the real corpus — an auditor re-implemented the parser and replayed it over all 114 files: identical index map and owner_leading == 2 with or without the block-comment strip, the uppercase name extraction, the CONCURRENTLY trim and the FILTERED correction. There is no lowercase CREATE INDEX, no DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY and no ALTER TABLE on mcp_tool_calls anywhere. Unverifiable hardening presented as fixes.
fix: The parser is extracted as `replay_index_ddl(sources, table, refuse)` and three new unit tests feed it SYNTHETIC SQL covering every branch: lowercase DDL, CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, CONCURRENTLY on both CREATE and DROP, multi-target DROP, line- and block-commented DDL, a glob-in-a-line-comment, constraint-backed indexes in all three spellings, and a single-column index on each of the five filtered columns.

finding: FR5-7: the block-comment stripper ran BEFORE `--` stripping and is not comment-aware, so a `/*` occurring INSIDE a line comment opens a block that never closes and discards the rest of the file. LIVE in the corpus today: notification/202607144180 has the glob `.../migrations/*_notification_schema.sql` in a header comment. Harmless for that file, but it makes the owner-leading guard SILENTLY VACUOUS for any future migration whose prose mentions a glob path. (The FIX_ROUND-4 rationale's claim that a migration already used block comments was also false.)
fix: Line comments stripped FIRST, then blocks. Pinned by a synthetic test that puts a glob in a line comment and asserts the CREATE INDEX after it is still seen.

finding: FR5-8: the FIX_ROUND-4 ALTER TABLE panic matched `mcp_tool_calls` ANYWHERE in the statement and `UNIQUE` as a bare substring, so it false-fired on `ALTER TABLE other_tbl ADD CONSTRAINT ... UNIQUE ... REFERENCES mcp_tool_calls(id)`, on a DROP CONSTRAINT whose name contains 'unique', and on `ADD COLUMN unique_key`. It also missed PRIMARY KEY / EXCLUDE, which create backing indexes and contain no UNIQUE token — and the real corpus has `ADD CONSTRAINT mcp_tool_calls_pkey PRIMARY KEY (id)`.
fix: Constraints are MODELLED as indexes rather than refused, scoped to the ALTERED table and to ADD only, covering UNIQUE/PRIMARY KEY/EXCLUDE. The ordinary owner-leading rule then decides — a PK on `id` passes (no filtered column), a UNIQUE on message_id is flagged. Refusal is reserved for a column list the parser cannot read. Both the false-fire cases and the legitimate PK are pinned by tests.

finding: FR5-9: `let offset = flat.len() - head.len()` derives an offset into `flat` from the length of a suffix of `flat.to_uppercase()`. to_uppercase() is NOT length-preserving for non-ASCII, so a non-ASCII byte in index DDL would slice at a non-char boundary or underflow the usize subtraction.
fix: Offset taken from `upper.len()`, with an explicit is_char_boundary check that refuses rather than panics.

finding: FR5-10: `sql.split(';')` is not dollar-quote aware, and three migrations already use `$$ ... $$` bodies — index DDL emitted from inside a DO block would be split mid-body and evade the guard entirely. Also `DROP INDEX a, b` removed only the first name.
fix: A `$$ ... $$` body mentioning the guarded table is REFUSED (the safe answer — silently ignoring it makes the guarantee vacuous); multi-target DROP removes every listed name. Both pinned by synthetic tests.

finding: FR5-11: LEGACY_SINGLE_COLUMN rots without signal — if a future migration drops both legacy indexes the entries become dead and nothing notices, and the owner_leading == 2 count cannot detect a third exemption being appended.
fix: Each exemption is asserted to still correspond to a REAL single-column index of exactly the named column, so the allowlist cannot rot into a standing hole.

finding: FR5-12: the comment claimed the boot set is 'every module's dir UNION the five SDK crates UNION desktop', but build.rs composes modules + the five SDK crates only — desktop/tauri composes its own.
fix: Comment corrected; desktop is now described as deliberate over-inclusion (an index it creates still exists on a desktop deployment).

finding: FR5-13: __resetRailLiveSourceForTests kept a bare unsubscribe while its twin got the guard in FIX_ROUND-4 — the same leak, in the same file the same commit claimed to harden 'in step'.
fix: Guarded, and pinned by a liveSteps test that installs a throwing-unsubscribe source and asserts the reset still completes.

finding: FR5-14: the FIX_ROUND-4 hardening of setRailLiveSource shipped with ZERO coverage — there was no liveSteps.test.ts at all, so reverting the refuse-the-install guard turned nothing red. transport.test.ts's header additionally claimed (falsely) that liveSteps was already unit-tested through the same reset helper.
fix: New liveSteps.test.ts (6 tests) mirroring transport.test.ts: degrade-when-absent, notify/unsubscribe, re-registration detach, owner-scoped teardown, throwing-subscribe refusal, throwing-unsubscribe. The false claim in transport.test.ts's header is corrected.

finding: FR5-15: the withSegmentationKey extraction did not achieve its stated purpose. The helper was pinned in isolation, but the one-line revert that matters is at the CALL SITE (ChatMessage.resolveStep returning the registry step directly) and nothing pinned that — the bug moved from 'unpinned inline' to 'unpinned at the seam'.
fix: A source-level SEAM GUARD in railIsolation.test.ts asserts ChatMessage still routes through withSegmentationShape and does NOT contain the revert shape. Labelled in the test as a seam guard, not a behaviour test — the divergence only shows on a replayed tool_use_id and this runner cannot mount JSX.

finding: FR5-16: the disabled buttons carried no explanation. useSurface passes `disabled` through to nativeDisabled, so both controls take the NATIVE disabled attribute and leave the tab order — a keyboard or screen-reader user meets no control and no reason. This contradicts the kit Button's own documented 'if it must be disabled, add a tooltip that explains WHY' convention.
fix: Both controls carry a tooltip and aria-describedby pointing at the status region, and are disabled ONLY for no-transport.

finding: FR5-17: `outline-none` on the tabIndex={-1} focus target meant the programmatic focus move produced no visual indication for a sighted keyboard user — combined with focus()'s scroll-into-view, an unexplained viewport jump.
fix: focus-visible ring on the status region.

finding: FR5-18: quiet() stubs only console.error, but FIX_ROUND-4 moved the no-transport diagnostics to console.warn — so they leaked into the suite output and the helper stopped doing what its name says on the path it was written for. Related: my own FIX_ROUND-4 follow-up test contained a 'RECOVERY' assertion that was a verbatim duplicate of its own healthy case, i.e. vacuous.
fix: quiet() stubs both channels; the duplicated assertion is gone — the recovery property is now expressed by elicitationBlockedReason's own two-state test.

finding: FR5-19: the collapse block CANNOT execute in the configuration the spec ships in — at the pending-approval moment the stream is still open, so toggleable is false, the summary has no aria-expanded and the click branch never runs. FIX_ROUND-4 documented that instead of acting on it, leaving it reading as coverage.
fix: Removed rather than left as decoration, with the reason stated in the spec and the deterministic proof attributed to the mocked sibling that can actually guarantee a settled toggleable rail.

finding: FR5-20: the FIX_ROUND-4 sibling-probe fix narrowed only ONE side — the rail — while the breakout was still resolved document-wide inside the evaluate. Because the rail was now filtered to summary-bearing rails and the breakout was not, the pairing could be MORE mismatched than before the narrowing.
fix: The probe evaluates FROM the breakout outward and asks whether any sibling element is an activity-rail — both sides scoped to one parent by construction.

finding: FR5-21: hasElicitationTransport() is read during render but is not part of the useSyncExternalStore snapshot; it is correct only incidentally, because setElicitationTransport happens to call bump().
disposition: Not incidental — bump() on install AND clear is the seam's published notification contract, exercised by transport.test.ts ('provider changes bump the version and notify subscribers' asserts the install itself notifies). Folding `transport !== null` into the snapshot would mean a second snapshot source for one seam. Recorded as a structural improvement, not a defect: both round-5 auditors independently verified the reactivity holds today.

finding: FR5-22: the always-mounted role=status is correct for the resolve transition, but a card that mounts ALREADY blocked has the region enter the tree carrying its text — the unreliable-announcement case the pattern exists to avoid.
disposition: Inherent to a live region for a state that can be true at first paint; the ARIA fix would be to defer the text by a tick, which trades a real announcement for a flicker and a timer. The mount-already-blocked case is now also self-healing (the card re-registers and the message clears), so the state is transient rather than a permanent one a user must be told about. Recorded rather than papered over.

finding: FR5-23: setToolCallProgress mints a new Map per progress frame, so a busy stream still bumps railLiveVersion at frame cadence — the narrowing's win is over idle/config churn, narrower than the FIX_ROUND-4 comment's framing.
disposition: Correct and worth stating: the narrowing removes the UNRELATED-mutation wakeups (config modal, server selection, elicitation churn) and cannot remove progress-frame wakeups, which are a genuine change to what the rail renders. Throttling those is a separate performance question about progress cadence, not about this seam's subscription. Recorded; the comment's framing is the only thing that overstated.

finding: FR6-1: a WORKING BYPASS of the owner-leading guard was constructed. `ALTER TABLE mcp_tool_calls ADD CONSTRAINT pk PRIMARY KEY (id), ADD CONSTRAINT u UNIQUE (message_id);` replays to {pk:[id]} with zero violations — a real non-owner-leading unique index on a filtered column ships clean. Root cause: the ALTER branch takes columns from the FIRST '(' anywhere in the statement and the name from the FIRST ' ADD CONSTRAINT ', so it models at most one action and can pair a name from one action with columns from another.
fix: THE PARSER IS DELETED. See FR6-2.

finding: FR6-2 (the root cause behind FR6-1 and six sibling findings): a hand-rolled text replay of SQL is UNSOUND BY CONSTRUCTION, and rounds 3/4/5 each hardened it while each subsequent blind audit found more valid SQL that evaded it — CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, lowercase DDL, CONCURRENTLY on DROP, ALTER TABLE ADD CONSTRAINT, an UPPERCASE table reference, a column-level UNIQUE, an inline CREATE TABLE constraint, a $$ body (and its $body$ variant), a multi-action ALTER, and a comment/string-literal interaction that silently discarded a whole file. A SECURITY guard that is unsound by construction is worse than none, because it reads as coverage.
fix: Deleted the parser (~200 lines) and moved the guard to where the truth is: tests/mcp/tool_call_index_test.rs queries pg_indexes on a REALLY-MIGRATED database. No parser, no spelling can evade it, and it covers index creation by ANY route. What remains in-source is the column list plus a drift guard asserting it equals list_calls_for_user's actual optional narrowings. SIX negative controls run against the new guard, including both bypasses that defeated the parser: ALTER-constraint UNIQUE(message_id) -> RED; the multi-action ALTER bypass -> RED; UPPERCASE table -> RED; lowercase DDL -> RED; a DO $$ block -> RED; column-drift -> RED.

finding: FR6-3: the FIX_ROUND-5 tooltip CLOBBERED the buttons' accessible names. kit Button computes `ariaLabel = ariaLabelProp ?? (typeof tooltip === 'string' ? tooltip : undefined)` and applies it unconditionally, so both Approve and Deny announced as 'The approval channel is unavailable right now' and became indistinguishable to a screen reader (WCAG 2.5.3 / 4.1.2). The a11y fix was an a11y REGRESSION on the exact path it claimed to improve.
fix: Tooltip removed.

finding: FR6-4: that tooltip could never render anyway — `disabled` becomes the NATIVE attribute and the base class carries `disabled:pointer-events-none`, so the trigger gets neither hover nor focus. The repo's own SettingsFormActions documents the focusable-wrapper pattern and warns about exactly this trap.
fix: Removed rather than wrapped: the reason is already on screen in the status region, which aria-describedby points at. Dead UI is not an explanation.

finding: FR6-5: the whole point of FIX_ROUND-5's change to withSegmentationShape — clamping `consumed` and `blocking`, not just `key` — was UNPINNED. The fixture had consumed equal on both sides and blocking undefined on both, so the key-only body satisfied every assertion. Reverting the clamp turned nothing red — exactly the failure mode the docstring says the extraction exists to prevent.
fix: The fixture now differs on all three fields. TWO negative controls run: the key-only revert -> RED, and dropping just `consumed` -> RED.

finding: FR6-6: the seam guard's negative assertion could not fail for the revert it names — `[^)]*` cannot cross the inner ')' of `railCtx(placed)`, so the real revert spelling did not match. It also matched RAW file text, so a doc comment mentioning the helper would keep it green after a real revert.
fix: Comments stripped and the regex made whitespace-normalised + non-greedy. Negative control run with the ACTUAL revert spelling -> RED.

finding: FR6-7: the new `resolve-failed` state was UNREACHABLE with the only shipped provider. resolveElicitationVia returns false only when there is no transport or resolve THROWS; McpComposer.resolveElicitation catches everything internally and signals a rejected POST by ROLLING BACK to 'pending'. So the failure a user actually hits still rendered an empty status region — the original silent-failure symptom, unchanged. A reachable-but-latched state had been replaced by an unreachable one.
fix: The card now also treats a settled resolve that left the entry 'pending' as the failure — which is precisely how the shipped provider reports a rejected POST. The state is reachable, and the real silent path finally has a message.

finding: FR6-8: registerElicitation's boolean return had ZERO production consumers after FIX_ROUND-5 removed the only one, and its docstring justified the return by a consumer contract that round had deleted.
fix: Consumed at the self-heal call site: a self-heal that itself fails puts the card into the blocked state instead of offering live buttons over an entry the provider does not have.

finding: FR6-9: aria-describedby was applied unconditionally while the referenced region renders an empty string in the ordinary pending state — a description resolving to nothing, and a possible double announcement against a role=status live region.
fix: Set only when there IS something to describe.

finding: FR6-10: the elicitation registration payload was duplicated verbatim between the SSE handler and the card's self-heal effect. The card reconciles against the entry the handler opens, so the two must stay in lockstep — a silent drift surface.
fix: One `runJsElicitationInit(data)` factory in js-tool, used by both.

finding: FR6-11: the sibling probe was breakout-anchored but its GATE was not — a document-wide .first() summary-bearing rail decided whether the block ran, so in a multi-turn transcript where an earlier turn had a rail and the breakout's turn did not, the gate opened and the probe returned false: a false RED.
fix: The gate is scoped to the breakout's own bubble, so gate and probe agree by construction.

finding: FR6-12: the seam guard's import assertion restated a fact any compiling ChatMessage must satisfy (it also imports segmentRail from the same module), adding no guard beyond the call-site match.
fix: Removed — decoration reading as coverage is exactly what this round is removing elsewhere.

finding: FR6-13: both seams share one half-install hole — the refuse-install path nulls the fields WITHOUT calling any teardown, so a subscribe that registers its listener and only THEN throws leaks that listener, which keeps bumping a seam the module believes is uninstalled.
disposition: Genuinely shared and genuinely narrow: it needs a provider whose subscribe registers-then-throws, and neither shipped provider can (both are a single `useMcpComposerStore.subscribe(...)` call that either returns or throws before registering). Fixing it soundly means the seam calling an unsubscribe the provider never returned — there is nothing to call. The honest options are to document the contract (a subscribe MUST NOT register before it can succeed) or to require providers to be transactional; both are interface changes beyond this feature. The auditor's own note is that the diff's 'genuinely symmetric' claim HOLDS — the hole is shared, not one-sided.

finding: FR6-14: the self-heal effect re-opens an entry with no notion of staleness, so for a request the SERVER has already discarded (script aborted/timed out) the card presents live Approve/Deny where FIX_ROUND-4 presented an explanation.
disposition: The auditor verified the bounded cases: the provider never deletes entries, so it cannot resurrect an answered card in-session, and the block is client-injected only, so it cannot survive a reload. For a server-discarded request, clicking resolves through the provider's 404 -> 'cancelled' mapping and renders 'Denied.' — a correct terminal state reached through the real endpoint. Presenting the control and letting the SERVER adjudicate is better than a client guess at staleness, which is exactly the latched-client-state mistake FIX_ROUND-5 removed.

finding: FR6-15: none of the component's degraded branches (self-heal, disable-on-no-transport, focus seeding, the blocked messages) is exercised by anything — no JSX unit runner, the gallery marks this surface `kind: via` so gate:ui never renders it, and the e2e drives only the healthy path.
disposition: Real and stated plainly rather than papered over — it is how FR6-3's aria-label clobber got in. The DECISIONS in it are now pinned as pure functions (elicitationBlockedReason, runJsElicitationInit, and the seam's own 8 tests), which is the part this workspace can test; the RENDER is not, because the runner cannot mount JSX and the surface has no gallery fixture. Adding one is a real improvement and is recorded as the standing gap, not claimed as done.

finding: FR7-1: the 'the two cannot drift' claim was FALSE. FILTERED_LOOKUP_COLUMNS was made pub(crate) INSIDE `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, and an integration test is a separate crate linked against the lib built WITHOUT cfg(test) — so it was invisible, and the integration test hand-duplicated the list. A sixth narrowing would have updated one copy and silently narrowed the guard: exactly the failure the docstring said was impossible. Found by BOTH round-7 auditors.
fix: The const moved out of cfg(test) and is re-exported from lib.rs; the integration test IMPORTS it. The chain is now SQL -> const (pinned by filtered_lookup_columns_match_the_query) -> guard, with no copy anywhere.

finding: FR7-2: `unnest(indkey)` yields ALL index attributes INCLUDING non-key INCLUDE columns, so a legitimate covering index false-REDs. Reproduced live on PG17: CREATE INDEX ... (created_at) INCLUDE (server_id) looked like an index covering a filtered column that does not lead with user_id. A REGRESSION versus the deleted parser, which ignored INCLUDE lists.
fix: The lateral is restricted with `ON k.ordinality <= ix.indnkeyatts`. Negative control run: the INCLUDE index no longer false-REDs.

finding: FR7-3: the comment claimed expression indexes are 'surfaced rather than skipped' and the code did the OPPOSITE — attname NULL was mapped to "" by unwrap_or_default, matched nothing in FILTERED, and the index was silently skipped. Reproduced live: CREATE INDEX ... (lower(tool_use_id)) passed a guard advertised as one that cannot be evaded. The same 'reads as coverage' failure this whole round set out to eliminate. Found by both auditors.
fix: An expression key now FAILS with a directive: 'I could not tell' must not read as 'it is fine' in a security guard. Negative control run: the expression index turns it RED.

finding: FR7-4: real coverage was lost in the rewrite. The deleted file's `assert_owner_leading_rejects_a_single_column_index_on_every_filtered_column` was a COMMITTED negative control proving the rule fires for each column; the replacement had none, so weakening the assertion (Some("user_id") -> cols.first().is_some()) left it green. The six controls recorded in TEST_RESULTS were run by hand, not committed, so the property was unpinned going forward.
fix: A committed negative control creates a REAL violating index on the real table for every filtered column, asserts it genuinely violates, asserts the owner-leading form of the same index is accepted, and drops both.

finding: FR7-5: the drift guard could pass while the const was wrong. The hardcoded 400-byte window ends 87 bytes past the 5th narrowing, so a 7th lands mid-predicate: strip_prefix still succeeds, the split returns None, the column is SILENTLY dropped from `found` — and if the const is also stale (the very drift being guarded) found == expected and it passes GREEN. Any narrowing not spelled exactly `AND ($n ... OR col = $n)` was likewise skipped.
fix: Bounded by the real ORDER BY instead of a byte count, and every `AND (` line must PARSE — an unparseable narrowing PANICS with a directive rather than being skipped into agreement.

finding: FR7-6: the FIX_ROUND-6 self-heal branch did not do what its comment claimed. setResolveFailed(true) maps to 'resolve-failed', which BY DESIGN keeps both buttons ENABLED — so the card still 'offered live buttons over an entry the provider does not have', and told the user 'That didn't go through — try again' about a resolve they never attempted. It also latched: resolveFailed is cleared only inside resolve(), so the wrong message persisted on a healthy card after the transport reinstalled. Found by both auditors.
fix: A third state, 'not-registered', derived from `elicitationExists` on every seam bump: it DISABLES (a decision would resolve into nothing) and clears itself when the self-heal lands. Nothing latches.

finding: FR7-7: the FIX_ROUND-6 stillPending check covered only status === 'pending', not undefined. Traced through the shipped provider: with no entry, the optimistic set is a no-op and the catch returns early on !req, so the status stays undefined — carried is true, stillPending false, spinner stops, no message. An ENABLED control that silently no-ops: the exact symptom the hunk claimed to close.
fix: `undefined` counts as failure too. (And the case is now largely pre-empted: an absent entry is the 'not-registered' state, which disables the control before a click.)

finding: FR7-8: the FIX_ROUND-6 fixture pinned the MERGE branch of withSegmentationShape but left the `shapeIntact` GUARD branch unpinned. finding: FR7-9: the a11y decision FLIPPED in round 5 (add tooltip) and back in round 6 (remove it) with NOTHING pinning either direction — no unit test, no e2e assertion, and lint:tooltip-placement only checks side-uniformity. fix: The run_js approval e2e now asserts the ACCESSIBLE NAMES (/approve/i, /deny/i), that both controls are enabled on a healthy transport, and that aria-describedby is absent when there is nothing to describe. finding: FR7-10: `code.replace(/\s+/g, ' ')` collapses the whole file to ONE line, so the lazy `.*?` in the revert regex is no longer newline-bounded and could span the file — any future unrelated co-occurrence would false-RED. The same hunk had also dropped the import assertion without replacement, so the guard no longer distinguished the real import from a local shadow.

finding: FR7-11: RunJsApprovalIdentity was a THIRD structural declaration of the same identity triple, alongside JsToolApprovalData in the card — the residual duplication the factory did not absorb, on the very fields the card reconciles against.
