finding: FR7-12: `let _ = legacy_cols;` was a dead binding — `find` had already matched on the column vector.
fix: Replaced with `.any(...)`, which expresses the same thing without the discard.

finding: FR7-13: `assert_eq!(seen_legacy, LEGACY.len())` made the security-CORRECT action fail — dropping one of the legacy single-column indexes (the shape the rule condemns) turned the guard RED.
fix: Relaxed to `<=`: exemptions may SHRINK, never grow. The vacuity concern it was covering is already carried by `checked >= 2`.

finding: FR7-14: the query had no pg_namespace restriction and grouped by relname, so a same-named relation in another schema could merge its attributes into one ambiguous array.
fix: Scoped to the `public` schema and grouped by index OID.

finding: FR7-15: the deleted unit test deliberately over-included desktop/tauri/migrations; the replacement runs against the SERVER template, so a desktop-only migration adding a bad index on mcp_tool_calls is no longer covered by any test.
disposition: Latent, and verified so by the auditor: nothing under desktop/tauri/migrations touches mcp_tool_calls today. Covering it means a second full TestServer boot on the desktop template purely for one SELECT — the guard already costs ~3s for that reason. Recorded as the residual scope, with the mitigation that the desktop binary applies the server's merged set (so any index authored in a SERVER migration IS covered on desktop too); only a desktop-EXCLUSIVE migration is outside.

finding: FR7-16: because the exemption keys on name + column vector, a future migration could launder a NEW non-owner-leading single-column index past the guard by reusing a legacy index NAME.
disposition: Inherent to any name-based exemption, and the alternative (keying on index OID or creation time) is not stable across a rebuilt test database. The realistic bound is that re-creating `idx_mcp_tool_calls_server` over `server_id` is EXACTLY the pre-existing index the exemption names — reusing the name over a DIFFERENT column set is already caught by the column-vector pin. Recorded rather than papered over.

finding: FR7-17: the guard moved from a filesystem-only unit test (<1ms) to one that boots a full TestServer (~3s measured) solely to run a pg_indexes SELECT, because the harness has no DB-only entry point.
disposition: The auditor's own verdict: 'correct tradeoff for soundness'. A DB-only harness entry point is a change to SHARED test infrastructure, which B3 forbids doing to serve one feature's problem. ~3s buys a guard that cannot be evaded by a SQL spelling, against a parser that was evaded seven times.

finding: FR8-1: the committed 'negative control' controlled NOTHING. It created a violating index and judged it with its OWN local helper — two Postgres tautologies — never invoking a single line of the guard. Both round-8 auditors RAN the exact mutation its own docstring named (assert_eq!(cols.first(), Some("user_id")) -> assert!(cols.first().is_some())) and BOTH tests stayed green. Zero mutation coverage for the guard, while reading as coverage.
fix: The rule is extracted as `assert_owner_leading(rows)` and the control drives it under catch_unwind on the live catalog. RE-RAN the same mutation: the control now FAILS with 'THE RULE DID NOT REJECT a single-column index on the filtered column `server_id`'.

finding: FR8-2: `assert!(seen_legacy <= LEGACY.len())` was UNFALSIFIABLE — relnames are unique per schema and rows are grouped by OID, so it could never exceed the length. It had REPLACED the only anti-rot check. Auditor RAN a stale allowlist entry naming a non-existent index: GREEN. A stale exemption is a standing hole that silently re-exempts any future index re-created under that name.
fix: Existence is REQUIRED again, with the shrink objection answered in the message: dropping a legacy index means deleting its exemption in the same change — two lines of hygiene, and an exemption for an index that no longer exists protects nothing and can only launder a future one. Re-ran the stale entry: RED.

finding: FR8-3: the restored import assertion checked only that ChatMessage imports SOMETHING from the segmentation module — and it already imports segmentRail and PlacedRailStep from it. Auditor RAN the mutation (drop withSegmentationShape from the import, add a local function of the same name, keep segmentRail): 6 passed. The comment claimed 'a locally-defined shadow cannot satisfy the call check'; the shadow satisfied it.
fix: Asserts the NAMED specifier is imported from that module. Re-ran the shadow mutation: RED.

finding: FR8-4: the e2e accessible-name assertion could not catch the regression it cited, and MY RECORDED CONTROL WAS MIS-DESIGNED. FIX_ROUND-5's tooltip was CONDITIONAL on the degraded state; this spec only ever reaches the healthy state, where the tooltip is undefined and the name is 'Approve'. Re-adding FIX_ROUND-5's code verbatim leaves it GREEN — the RED I recorded came from an UNCONDITIONAL tooltip, which is not the regression.
fix: The property is pinned by a SOURCE guard ('no tooltip on a Button that can be disabled'), run against FIX_ROUND-5's verbatim CONDITIONAL form: RED. The e2e assertions are kept for what they do pin (accessible names, conditional aria-describedby). TEST_RESULTS.md is CORRECTED rather than left claiming a control that did not hold — the reason the e2e cannot be the guard (no spec can reach a state needing mcp's transport absent mid-conversation) is stated in the test.

finding: FR8-5: `not-registered` LATCHED with both controls disabled — the THIRD latch this card has grown. A failed register returns false and bumps nothing, so no re-render, no dep change, and the self-heal effect never retried; resolve() also early-returned. Strictly less recoverable than FIX_ROUND-6, which at least left the controls enabled. Both auditors.
fix: TWO changes, and the second is the one that matters. (1) `seamVersion` is a dep, so a failed register retries on the next seam change. (2) ONLY the impossible state disables: `elicitationIsUnactionable` returns true for `no-transport` alone. The through-line of all three latches is that a state the user could still act through was disabled — so the rule is now written down and pinned by its own test.

finding: FR8-6: disabling on `not-registered` removed a recovery path that WORKED. McpComposer.resolveElicitation POSTs unconditionally — the optimistic set is a no-op with no local entry, but ApiClient.Mcp.respondToElicitation still fires and the suspended server-side script still resumes. Before the hunk a click genuinely resolved the approval; after it, both buttons were disabled and resolve() early-returned.
fix: `not-registered` no longer disables, and its copy changed from 'Reopening this request… if it stays this way, reload' to 'Reopening this request — you can still answer it.' The message now matches what the control does.

finding: FR8-7: the drift guard's 'fails loudly' property was conditional on FORMATTING. The panic path was reachable only for lines already starting with `AND (`; an auditor verified two ordinary spellings skipped SILENTLY — a narrowing appended to the `WHERE user_id = $1` line, and two narrowings on one line — each leaving a stale const in agreement and the test GREEN.
fix: Splits on the `AND (` TOKEN over the whitespace-flattened clause, so formatting is irrelevant, and every fragment must parse. Control run: moving an existing narrowing onto the WHERE line and removing its column from the const is now RED (it was the silent case before).

finding: FR8-8: the expression-key assert ran BEFORE the FILTERED-membership filter, so it hard-failed for ANY expression key on the table — including a fully COMPLIANT index. `CREATE INDEX ... (user_id, lower(tool_name))` leads with user_id and covers no filtered column, yet turned the guard RED: the same false-RED class the INCLUDE fix removed one round earlier. The remediation its message offered had no implementation.
fix: The question is asked ONLY when the index does not already lead with user_id — i.e. only when the guard genuinely cannot decide. Two controls run: the compliant expression index passes; a non-compliant one (lower(tool_use_id)) still turns it RED.

finding: FR8-9: registerElicitation's boolean has zero production consumers again, and its docstring still described a consumer contract that no longer exists.
fix: The docstring now says what is true: the return is a DIAGNOSTIC, not the mechanism — a consumer that needs to know whether the entry exists asks the seam (elicitationExists), because that answer is LIVE while this one is a snapshot. Routing it through caller state is what produced a latch twice.

finding: FR8-10: the FIX_ROUND-7 per-line normalisation fixed a false-RED but introduced a false-GREEN — `[^\n]*?` cannot cross a newline, so a line-WRAPPED revert was no longer detected, whereas the whole-file form had caught it.
fix: Scoped to the `resolveStep` DECLARATION and collapsed within it, which gives both properties. BOTH revert spellings run: inline -> RED, line-wrapped -> RED.

finding: FR8-11: the parser anchors on the first `FROM mcp_tool_calls` and bounds on its `ORDER BY`, covering only the SELECT half; the COUNT half repeats the identical predicate list and is never parsed, so a narrowing added there alone is invisible.
disposition: Bounded and already covered from the other side: `filters_never_drop_the_owner_predicate` (TEST-17) asserts the predicate list appears in BOTH statements, so a narrowing present in COUNT but absent from SELECT fails there. The residual is a narrowing added ONLY to COUNT — which cannot change what rows are returned, only the total, and would be caught by the pagination tests. Parsing both halves would mean two anchors and a divergence check between them, which is the same duplication this round removed elsewhere.

finding: FR8-12: `assert!(FILTERED.contains(&col))` was tautological — `col` comes from `for col in FILTERED`.
fix: Removed in the rewrite; the control now asserts the fixture index is actually IN THE CATALOG, which is a real precondition.

finding: FR8-13: the `leading_column_of` helper swallowed every query error via `.ok()`, so a broken helper query read as 'the fixture correctly violates the rule'.
fix: The helper is gone entirely — the control drives the real rule over the real catalog rows, and `index_rows` uses `.expect(...)`.

finding: FR8-14: the `after === undefined` term is effectively unreachable with the shipped provider and masked by `not-registered`'s higher precedence, while the comment presented it as fixing an observed path.
fix: Comment corrected to say it is DEFENSIVE, and to say why it is kept: the seam's contract permits `status()` to return undefined, so a conforming provider that deletes on resolve must not read as success.

finding: FR8-15: three assert/panic messages carried literal ~20-space runs from a reflow, visible in real failure output — the messages a maintainer reads at the moment a security guard fails.
fix: Collapsed.

finding: FR8-16: the negative control boots a second full TestServer (~1.3s of ~3.0s) to assert two Postgres tautologies.
fix: The tautologies are gone — it now drives the real rule under catch_unwind, so the second server buys genuine mutation coverage of a security guard rather than nothing.

finding: FR8-17: `extends RunJsApprovalIdentity` dedupes the TYPE but not the PRODUCER — the SSE handler still builds the block as a bare object literal cast `as unknown as MessageContent`, so there is no compile-time link between what it writes and what the card reads.
disposition: Correct, and the residual is structural rather than local: the cast exists because the streaming block is assembled as a `MessageContent` whose `content` is an untyped JSON payload — the same shape every chat extension uses to inject a streaming block. Typing that channel is a chat-core change affecting every extension, not a js-tool fix, and doing it here would be exactly the cross-module reach this feature exists to remove. The three identity FIELDS are now single-sourced through the factory both sides call, which closes the drift that is actionable from here.

finding: FR9-1: MY OWN whitespace 'cleanup' in FIX_ROUND-8 destroyed the file's indentation — 222 lines collapsed to a single leading space, spanning production SQL literals and sqlx macro argument lists, ~466 of the diff's changed lines. It drowned the one real change in noise on a file whose whole purpose is owner-scoping guarantees, and re-baselined the SQL TEXT that this same file's source-parsing guards match against. No gate catches it (cargo fmt is not clean repo-wide), so it would have persisted. Found independently by both round-9 auditors.
fix: Reverted properly: the file restored from the round-7 commit and ONLY the intended parser change re-applied. The diff vs round 7 is now 22 insertions / 10 deletions instead of 466 lines of churn, and 0 lines carry a single-space indent. The two message strings that genuinely needed repair were fixed surgically, by exact match, not by a regex over the whole file — which is what caused this.

finding: FR9-2: the tooltip source guard — the SOLE pin for an a11y regression that already shipped once — was evaded by three ordinary spellings, all MUTATION-VERIFIED GREEN: boolean-shorthand `<Button disabled tooltip=…>` (the predicate required an `=`, and the shorthand is the most natural spelling for a permanently-disabled control); a spread carrying `disabled`; and a `>` inside any earlier quoted attribute, which truncated the brace-depth scan before it saw either prop.
fix: The scanner tracks quotes as well as braces, and the predicate accepts assignment, boolean shorthand and a spread. All three evasions re-run: each now RED.

finding: FR9-3: `try { readFileSync } catch { continue }` made the guard silently vacuous the moment a scanned file was renamed — mutation-verified: moving the file WITH a violation in it left the test green. Both auditors noted this is the same standing-hole shape the SAME branch had just condemned on the Rust side, where the argument was that tolerating absence 'protects nothing and can only ever launder a future one'. The reasoning was not applied to the guard's own file list.
fix: The catch is removed: a rename now fails loudly. Re-run: the moved file turns it RED.

finding: FR9-4: the round's headline rule ('only the impossible state disables') was pinned as a PURE PREDICATE but NOT at the two JSX call sites that render it. Mutation-verified: changing both `disabled` props back to `disabled={blocked !== null}` — re-introducing the exact FIX_ROUND-7 latch — left the entire UI unit suite, check:state-matrix and tsc green.
fix: A source guard asserts every `disabled` prop on the approval controls is exactly `elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)`. The latch mutation is now RED.

finding: FR9-5: the resolveStep guard sliced a HARDCODED 400-char window. Mutation-verified: an ordinary multi-branch body puts the revert spelling at offset 417, past the window, and the test stays GREEN while the import and call checks are satisfied by the other branch. An auditor noted this is the same defect class the FIX_ROUND-7 comment IN THIS VERY FILE condemns on the Rust side ('bounded by the real ORDER BY, not a hardcoded 400-byte window').
fix: Bounded by the declaration's REAL end (scan to the next top-level declaration) and the declaration itself must call the helper. The multi-branch revert is now RED.

finding: FR9-6: adding `seamVersion` to the self-heal effect's deps makes termination depend on an invariant the ElicitationTransport contract does NOT state. Measured by an auditor against the real module under jsdom: the shipped provider terminates at 1 register / 2 renders (and 5 cards cost 5 registers), but a provider whose `register` notifies WITHOUT making `has(id)` true — permitted by the published contract — spins to ~54 calls until React's update-depth bail-out, with the resulting error swallowed and MISLABELLED by this module's own catch.
fix: Both halves. The contract now REQUIRES `register` to make `has(id)` true synchronously before any notification for it, with the measurement as the rationale; and the consumer bounds itself at 3 attempts, so a non-conforming provider degrades instead of spinning.

finding: FR9-7: two hunks of FIX_ROUND-8 contradicted each other. It stopped disabling on `not-registered` because the provider POSTs unconditionally — and in exactly that state the provider holds no entry, so the status stays `undefined`, which the `after === undefined` term recorded as a FAILURE. A SUCCESSFUL approve was therefore marked failed. Masked only by `not-registered` outranking `resolve-failed` in the classifier. Both auditors.
fix: The outcome is judged only when the provider HELD an entry to judge it by; with no entry the POST still went out and the script still resumed, so it is not a failure. `not-registered` already describes that card and the self-heal resolves it.

finding: FR9-8: all three blocked reasons rendered in `text-destructive`, including `not-registered` — which the same round redefined as transient, self-healing and explicitly answerable ('you can still answer it'). The semantic split introduced in the predicate was not carried into the styling, and DESIGN_SYSTEM.md reserves destructive for errors.
fix: `danger` only for the states that genuinely stop the user (`no-transport`, `resolve-failed`); `not-registered` renders as secondary, matching its own copy.

finding: FR9-9: a repo-wide kit/a11y invariant is implemented as a hand-rolled string scanner inside the rail-isolation test, reaching by hardcoded path into two other modules — while the repo already ships a TypeScript-AST lint framework (sdk/packages/config/src/lint/*.mjs, incl. tooltip-placement.mjs) wired into npm run check over BOTH workspaces, which would be repo-wide and immune to every evasion by construction.
disposition: Correct, and the right destination — but the lint framework lives in the `sdk` SUBMODULE, and this branch already carries one unpushed sdk commit that the orchestrator must land before the superproject pointer. Adding a lint rule there compounds that coordination, and B3 forbids reshaping shared infrastructure to serve one feature's problem. The local guard is now robust against all three proven evasions and fails loudly on rename, so the property is genuinely held today. Recorded as the correct follow-up with its destination named.

finding: FR9-10 (scope note, predates this branch): FILTERED_LOOKUP_COLUMNS covers only the optional NARROWINGS, so `idx_mcp_tool_calls_created` on plain `(created_at)` is never inspected — despite `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT` making it the most planner-attractive non-owner-leading index on the table, which is the harm shape migration 202607200200's own EXPLAIN narrative describes.
disposition: The auditor's own framing: a scope note, not a defect of this diff. The rule this branch introduced governs the FILTERED narrowings, and widening it to the ORDER BY column is a different (and larger) claim about the table's index strategy — `idx_mcp_tool_calls_user_created` already exists as the owner-leading form, so the question is whether the plain `(created_at)` index should be dropped, which is a migration decision for the mcp module rather than a rail change. Recorded with the evidence so it is actionable by whoever owns that call.

finding: FR10-1: ALL THREE production behaviour changes in FIX_ROUND-9 were unpinned. An auditor reverted all three at once (the healAttempts cap, the `hadEntry &&` failure judgement, the tone) and ran the full 843-test suite: the failing-file set was byte-identical to baseline. The only e2e exercises the healthy transport and never reaches a blocked state. Two of the three are described by the round's own comments as bug fixes — on a branch whose stated method is to pin every regression.
fix: Both decisions extracted as pure predicates (`elicitationIsError`, `resolveDidFail`) — the shape the seam already demonstrates, and the only shape this workspace can test since its runner cannot mount JSX. Two mutation controls run: reverting the tone rule -> RED; reverting the failure judgement -> RED.

finding: FR10-2: the tooltip guard had NO non-vacuity floor. It scans for the literal `<Button`, so a surface spelling its control anything else finds zero elements and passes. PROVEN: renaming `<Button` to `<ApprovalButton` AND injecting the exact defect left all 8 tests green. Its own sibling guards against this with a `>= 2` floor; this one asserted nothing was found.
fix: Asserts each scanned surface renders at least one <Button>, with a message that says which of the two causes it is.

finding: FR10-3: the `catch { continue }` tolerance FIX_ROUND-9 removed — arguing 'a renamed file must fail, not silently pass' and that it 'did not deserve an exception here' — still stood verbatim 240 lines up in TEST-36, in the SAME file. PROVEN: renaming LiteratureToolResultCard.tsx and re-adding the forbidden import left all 8 tests green. The principle was applied to one of two identical constructs.
fix: Removed there too. Re-run: the rename now turns it RED.

finding: FR10-4: the call-site pin used EXACT STRING equality, which false-RED on behaviour-preserving refactors — proven for hoisting the value to a local and for renaming the local `blocked` — with a message ('must derive `disabled` from the seam predicate') that MISDIAGNOSED code still doing exactly that.
fix: A property, not a spelling: the card must use the seam predicate somewhere, and no element may re-derive `disabled` from the raw blocked reason. Three controls run — the hoist refactor is GREEN, and both latch forms (`disabled={blocked !== null}` and a later spread carrying it) are RED.

finding: FR10-5: the exact-expression pin was evadable by a JSX spread placed AFTER the conforming prop — later props win at runtime, so `{...{ disabled: blocked !== null }}` fully reverted the decision while both new tests stayed green. Self-inconsistent within the same hunk, since the sibling guard already treats a spread as reachable.
fix: The element-level check now rejects any `disabled` re-derived from `blocked !==`/`===`, in a prop OR a spread. Control run: spread-after -> RED.

finding: FR10-6: the new quote-tracking FALSE-POSITIVED on legitimate JSX — an apostrophe in JSX TEXT inside a prop expression (`icon={<span>Don't…`) was read as a string opener, swallowing the next element and failing with a misleading count. JSX text is not a JS string literal.
fix: Quotes are tracked only at brace depth 0 — the attribute list itself. Control run: the apostrophe no longer fires, and the quoted-`>` evasion it was added for is still RED.

finding: FR10-7: the declaration bound could be TOO LONG — it terminated only on a 2-indent const/function/return, so an `if`/`for`/`useEffect` following the declaration was swallowed and a `withSegmentationShape(` in a NEIGHBOURING statement satisfied the declaration-level check, reopening the 'merely the file' hole at a smaller radius.
fix: Terminates on ANY 2-indent construct.

finding: FR10-8: exhausting the heal budget left stale, actively-false copy. The effect returns early and the self-heal STOPS, but the card keeps rendering 'Reopening this request…' — a present-progressive claim about work that has ceased. The user is not hard-stuck (the controls stay live and still POST), but nothing signals that retrying stopped.
fix: A distinct message once the budget is spent: 'This request could not be reopened locally — you can still answer it, or reload the conversation.' It keeps the true clause and drops the false one.

finding: FR10-9: a doc comment directly contradicted the code three lines below it, and FIX_ROUND-9 created the contradiction — it deleted the `|| after === undefined` clause but left the paragraph explaining why that clause was KEPT. Alongside it, two near-verbatim FIX_ROUND-6 paragraphs sat back to back, leaving a 26-line comment stack over one `if`, three rounds of which described rules no longer in force.
fix: The stack is replaced by one paragraph that describes the CURRENT rule and names the two supersessions. Same treatment for a stale comment in transport.test.ts that said `not-registered` disables.

finding: FR10-10: `healAttempts` was a bare useRef never reset on `data.elicitation_id` change, so a component instance React reuses for a DIFFERENT elicitation inherits a spent budget and gets zero attempts. Also an unnamed magic number, with no note that the budget is per-MOUNT (scrolling the virtualized transcript silently grants a fresh one).
fix: Keyed to the elicitation id and reset on change; named `HEAL_BUDGET` with the rationale for the VALUE, not just for having a cap; and the per-mount scope is now stated as deliberate.

finding: FR10-11: the kit-a11y and elicitation-seam guards live in the rail-isolation test, whose own header defines it as the INV-1 guard — so a rename of JsToolApprovalContent.tsx now fails a test in chat/components/rail/, and the file's docstring no longer describes its contents.
disposition: Fair, and the destination named in FR9-9 is better still (the repo's AST lint framework, which would be repo-wide). Both moves are deferred for the same reason: the lint framework is in the `sdk` submodule this branch already has one unpushed commit in, and relocating the guards to per-module test files right before hand-off trades a real, mutation-proven property for churn in files the orchestrator is about to merge. Recorded with both destinations so the follow-up is unambiguous.

finding: FR10-12: the drift guard splits only on the `AND (` token, so a narrowing spelled without it — e.g. `AND COALESCE($9::uuid, branch_id) = branch_id` — is SILENTLY invisible rather than failing loudly, leaving the const in agreement and the index guard (scoped BY that const) blind to the new column. Narrower than the comment's claim: the comment's own literal examples DO fail loudly.
disposition: Bounded and honest about its shape: every narrowing in the query today, and every one the codebase writes, uses the `($n IS NULL OR col = $n)` idiom — which is itself pinned by `filters_never_drop_the_owner_predicate`. A narrowing that abandons the idiom entirely is a deliberate rewrite of the cross-user guard's shape, which that sibling test forces the author to confront. Making the parser total over arbitrary SQL is the unsound direction this branch already abandoned once, at length, for exactly this reason.

finding: FR11-1: the call-site guard ENUMERATED bad spellings, which is unbounded — and the enumeration missed most of them. Both auditors mutation-proved the FIX_ROUND-7 latch reintroducible as `disabled={!!blocked}` and `disabled={blocked != null}` with the suite GREEN (also `Boolean(blocked)`, `blocked ? true : false`). Only the literal `blocked !== null` fired. One auditor's verdict: the guard was 'strictly weaker than the round it supersedes, on the exact regression it is named for' — FIX_ROUND-9's exact-match killed every one of these mutants; FIX_ROUND-10 relaxed it to fix a false-RED and gave that away.
fix: Inverted to REQUIRE THE GOOD FORM: each `disabled` expression must route through `elicitationIsUnactionable`, directly or via one local const (so the hoist refactor stays legal), and a spread carrying `disabled` is refused outright since a later spread silently overrides the checked prop. Enumerating the bad is unbounded; requiring the good is not. Seven controls run: loose-equality, double-bang, Boolean(), ternary, spread-after -> each RED; the hoist refactor -> GREEN.

finding: FR11-2: the file-level `elicitationIsUnactionable(` check gave no cover, because it is satisfied by the NON-RENDERING call inside `resolve()`. Mutation-proven: replacing BOTH `disabled` props with the latch while leaving that call untouched left the suite green — both approval controls latched, no test failing.
fix: The check is per-ELEMENT now, on the actual `disabled` expression, so an unrelated call site cannot satisfy it.

finding: FR11-3: `resolveDidFail` and `elicitationIsError` were extracted in FIX_ROUND-10 on the explicit grounds that 'reverting the fix left the whole suite green' — and only the FUNCTIONS were pinned. Both auditors mutation-proved that reverting either at its CALL SITE was still green: the inline failure judgement marks a SUCCESSFUL approve as failed whenever the provider holds no entry, and the inline tone repaints a transient answerable state in destructive red. Each fix was one inline expression away from being undone.
fix: A call-site guard pins both: the tone must route through `elicitationIsError` and the judgement through `resolveDidFail`. Controls run: reverting the tone -> RED; reverting the judgement -> RED.

finding: FR11-4: `healExhausted` was derived by reading a REF during render while the ref is mutated inside the effect — so it was structurally one render behind, and in the very failure mode the component documents it never fired at all: a failed register bumps nothing, so nothing re-renders, so the exhausted copy could never appear and the present-progressive 'Reopening this request…' stayed on screen permanently. The active falsehood FIX_ROUND-10 removed survived in precisely the state it was written for. One auditor demonstrated it under real react-dom/jsdom. Reading a ref during render is also impure under StrictMode.
fix: `useState`, not a ref, with the attempt record in the effect's deps — so each failed attempt re-renders, the budget is actually reached, and the exhausted copy renders. Bounded by the budget.

finding: FR11-5: the `resolveDidFail` truth table asserted only combinations the implementation happens to produce — every `hadEntry:false` row paired with `after: undefined`, where both implementations agree. So deleting the `hadEntry &&` conjunct, the whole point of the function, SURVIVED. Both auditors, independently. The published contract permits `status()` to answer while `has()` is false, so the missing cell is reachable.
fix: The discriminating cell `{carried: true, hadEntry: false, after: 'pending'}` added, plus the terminal `cancelled` and `undefined` rows. Control run: dropping the conjunct is now RED.

finding: FR11-6: a comment claimed `not-registered` 'DISABLES the controls' — untrue since FIX_ROUND-8, and contradicted by the seam's own bolded 'Do NOT disable'. It is the IDENTICAL stale claim FIX_ROUND-10 explicitly corrected in the sibling test file, missed in the file whose behaviour it describes.
fix: Corrected, and it names the miss.

finding: FR11-7: moving quote tracking to depth 0 fixed the apostrophe false-RED but introduced a symmetric false-NEGATIVE — a `}` inside a string inside a prop expression decrements depth early and truncates the window, so a real violation after it is missed. Proven by differential harness: the OLD scanner caught it, the NEW one did not. The comment presented the change as a pure fix.
fix: Quotes tracked at EVERY depth again, with the apostrophe case handled precisely instead: inside a prop expression a `'` opens a string only in expression position, not when it follows a letter (JSX text). Both controls run: the brace-in-string violation is RED, the apostrophe is correctly GREEN.

finding: FR12-1: `routesThrough` required the good predicate to be PRESENT, not to DECIDE. Both auditors mutation-proved `disabled={elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked) || blocked !== null}` — the cheapest possible revert shape — green, along with a full semantic INVERSION `!elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)`, which disables the card in every recoverable state and enables it only where a click cannot leave the browser. One auditor also proved all three named historical regressions revertible SIMULTANEOUSLY with the suite green, i.e. the round added no net protection.
fix: `isExactly`: the whole expression must BE the call, or a local whose sole initializer is the call. Any `||`/`&&`/`?`/leading `!` means something else participates in the decision and the guard refuses rather than guesses. Six controls run: or-latch, inversion, tone-or, a hoist carrying a latch -> each RED; a Prettier-wrapped hoist -> GREEN.

finding: FR12-2: the tone pin took the FIRST `type={…}` anywhere in the file, so it did not pin the status region at all. Proven both ways: a conforming `type={}` on any earlier element made a full revert of the status region GREEN; and a behaviour-preserving `type="secondary"` -> `type={'secondary'}` on an unrelated element turned it RED with a misdiagnosing message — the identical false-RED-with-wrong-message failure round 10 diagnosed in round 9.
fix: Anchored to the element carrying `data-testid={statusId}`, scanned the way buttonProps scans a Button. Control run: the decoy-plus-revert is now RED.

finding: FR12-3: the failure-judgement pin asserted only that `resolveDidFail(` appeared inside an `if` — not that its result gates `setResolveFailed(true)`. Proven: adding `if (!hadEntry) setResolveFailed(true)` beside the conforming call fully re-introduces the FIX_ROUND-9 bug (a successful approve reported as failed) with the suite green.
fix: `setResolveFailed(true)` must occur EXACTLY ONCE and must be the direct consequent of the `resolveDidFail(...)` condition. Control run: a second judgement beside it -> RED.

finding: FR12-4 (a real behaviour regression I introduced in FIX_ROUND-11): adding `healAttempts` to the effect deps COLLAPSED the retry cadence. Every set allocates a new object, so the effect re-ran itself and burned the whole budget in one tick at mount — after which no later seam change could retry at all, the opposite of what FIX_ROUND-8 added the seam trigger for. An auditor measured it under real react-dom: OLD = 1 register at mount +1 per seam bump; NEW = 3 synchronously then 0 forever. Two in-file comments still described the old cadence.
fix: The count is carried by a REF for the effect (no dep, so the cadence survives) and mirrored into state for the render (which is what made the exhausted copy observable at all). The register call stays OUT of the state updater, which React may invoke twice under StrictMode.

finding: FR12-5: the local-hop regex used `[^\n]*`, confining the initializer to ONE line — so a Prettier-wrapped hoist (`const approvalControlsAreUnactionableRightNow =\n  elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)`) false-RED. The docstring claimed the hop 'keeps a hoist-to-a-const refactor legal'; the very refactor that motivates hoisting — a long name — was the one it rejected.
fix: Matched on whitespace-collapsed source with a negative lookahead for a following operator, so a wrapped initializer counts while `= pred(x) || latch` does not. Both controls run.

finding: FR12-6: the `apostropheInWord` heuristic only exempted an apostrophe preceded by an alphanumeric, so JSX text with a LEADING apostrophe (`'til`, `'90s`, `'em`) still opened a phantom string and ran the window to EOF, producing a false violation. The FIX_ROUND-11 comment claimed the case was 'handled precisely'.
fix: Keyed on the enclosing REGION instead of the neighbouring character: JSX text lives between a `>` and the next `<`, so an apostrophe there is prose whatever precedes it. Three controls run: `'til` and `'90s` correctly GREEN, the brace-in-string violation still RED.

finding: FR12-7: `indexOf('<Button')` prefix-matched `<ButtonGroup` / `<ButtonLink`, scanning a different component as if it were a Button.
fix: Requires a non-identifier character after the tag name. Control run: a `<ButtonGroup disabled tooltip>` is no longer scanned.

finding: FR12-8: two tests bound to `APPROVAL_SURFACES[0]` positionally, so inserting a third surface at index 0 would silently retarget them and leave the real surface unguarded.
fix: Named `APPROVAL_SURFACE_WITH_CONTROLS`, with the list built from it.

finding: FR12-9: the new guards pin js-tool's INTERNAL identifiers from inside the rail-isolation test, deepening that file's remit from 'which files exist and which props they carry' to 'which local variable names they use'.
disposition: Third time this has been raised (FR9-9, FR10-11, now FR12-9) and the answer is unchanged and deliberate: the right home is either a per-surface spec or the repo's AST lint framework, and the latter lives in the `sdk` submodule this branch already has one unpushed commit in. Relocating mutation-proven guards immediately before hand-off trades a held property for churn in files the orchestrator is about to merge. Recorded a third time so the follow-up is unambiguous rather than forgotten.

finding: FR13-1: FIX_ROUND-12's headline fix WAS NOT APPLIED. The comment says at length that `healAttempts` is 'deliberately NOT a dep', and the dep array still listed it — so the whole budget still burned in one tick at mount and no later seam change could retry, which is the exact regression the commit subject claimed to restore. BOTH auditors proved it under real React 19 + jsdom, with counterfactual measurements. My own error, undetected by any gate (lint:hooks does not check exhaustive-deps).
fix: The dep is removed. The cadence is 1 attempt at mount and one per later seam change, as FIX_ROUND-8 intended.

finding: FR13-2: `registerElicitation` was called TWICE per heal attempt — FIX_ROUND-12 added the call intending to hoist it out of the state updater and did not delete the original. Both auditors verified against the parent commit, which has exactly one. Each attempt therefore fired two seam bumps, re-rendering every mounted approval card twice and doubling the churn the mcp subscribe narrowing exists to avoid, and logged its degraded-path warnings twice. My own error.
fix: The duplicate is removed.

finding: FR13-3 (the ROOT CAUSE, and the reason this round stopped patching): the source guards parsed TypeScript with REGEXES, so every round closed one spelling and the next audit found another. Across rounds 8-13 the accumulated evasions were: boolean-shorthand `disabled`, a spread, a `>` inside a quoted attribute, `!!x`, `x != null`, `Boolean(x)`, `x ? true : false`, `pred(x) || latch`, `!pred(x)`, a `let` reassigned later, a hop with `=== false`, a second ternary branch reaching 'danger', a non-literal `setResolveFailed` argument, and a non-identifier argument to the predicate itself. Round 13 added four more (argument unpinned two ways, `let` reassignment, `lastAngle` never reset re-opening the quote hole). Enumerating spellings is unbounded — the exact mistake these guards' own docblock condemned in the guard they replaced.
fix: REWRITTEN ON THE TYPESCRIPT AST. The compiler is already a dependency (it runs on every npm run check), so the guards ask IT what the code says: a JSX attribute is distinguished from prose, a spread from a prop, and an expression's exact shape from a substring of it, all by construction. `isExactCall` requires a CallExpression with the right callee AND argument, or a `const` whose sole initializer is that call and which is never reassigned; the tone guard checks the WHOLE ternary; the judgement guard counts every non-`false` call and walks to its governing `if`. ALL 14 accumulated evasions were re-run against it: each RED. All 4 legitimate refactors (wrapped hoist, braced consequent, element-valued prop before the testid, apostrophes in JSX text) : each GREEN.

finding: FR13-4: seven comments misdescribed the code they annotate, two asserting the opposite of what shipped — including 'STATE, not a ref' sitting three lines above a newly added ref, and a StrictMode rationale for a change the diff did not make. An auditor called comment accuracy 'the worst' dimension of the round.
fix: The ref/state pair now has ONE comment explaining why BOTH exist and why they cannot diverge; the StrictMode note is reduced to what is true. The stale paragraphs in the test file went with the regex scanner they described.

finding: FR13-5: the tone guard's failure messages were inaccurate for failures it could actually produce — a behaviour-equivalent `resolved ? 'secondary' : ...` reported 'a transient state gets painted destructive-red', which is not what happened, and a `??` in the expression truncated the reported text mid-token.
fix: The AST version reports the exact node it rejected, and each assertion has its own message naming the shape it wanted.

finding: FR13-6: an unfounded past-tense claim ('`<ButtonGroup` ... were being scanned as if they were Buttons') — a tree-wide grep matched only the comment itself. The hardening was correct; the history was invented.
fix: Gone with the regex scanner. The AST matches the tag name exactly, so the class cannot arise and needs no claim about it.

finding: FR14-1: the AST rewrite walked to the enclosing `if` and checked its CONDITION but never which BRANCH the call was in — so `if (resolveDidFail(...)) {} else setResolveFailed(true)` passed. A one-token inversion that marks every SUCCESSFUL approve as failed. Both auditors proved it. This is a REGRESSION from round 13: the regex it replaced required adjacency and DID catch it.
fix: The judging call's span must lie inside `guard.thenStatement`. Control run: the else-inversion is RED.

finding: FR14-2: every guard inspected only the JSX `disabled` attribute, while the re-entrancy early-return in `resolve()` — which decides whether the POST actually happens — was unguarded. An auditor proved latching it there reintroduces the FIX_ROUND-4 bug in a WORSE form: the control still RENDERS enabled, so the user clicks, and the click silently no-ops with no visual signal at all. All 9 guards stayed green and tsc was clean.
fix: A tenth guard pins resolve()'s gate on the same seam predicate and forbids re-deriving from the raw blocked reason. Control run: the handler latch is RED.

finding: FR14-3: `isExactCall` matched the callee by TEXT and never resolved the binding, so the guard verified a NAME, not the seam function. Proven green (and tsc-clean) two ways: a same-named local function, and the same name imported from a sibling module. The auditor flagged the second as a plausible drift path, not merely adversarial.
fix: Each predicate must be IMPORTED from `core/elicitation/transport`, asserted on the import declarations. Control run: the local-predicate substitution is RED.

finding: FR14-4: asymmetric hardening — `isExactCall` was extended to check its argument, while the `resolveDidFail` governance check pinned only the callee and ignored arguments, so a constant-true call (`{carried: false, hadEntry: true, after: 'pending'}`) passed and made every approve show the failure copy.
fix: Every property of the signals object must be a shorthand or an identifier reference, never a literal. Control run: the constant-args call is RED.

finding: FR14-5: the guards hardcoded the local name `blocked` as the required argument, so a pure, type-clean rename false-RED both of them with a message ('a different argument changes which states disable') that is untrue for a rename.
fix: The argument is checked by BINDING — it must be the local initialised from `elicitationBlockedReason(...)` — so a rename is legal and a substituted expression is not. Control run: renaming `blocked` to `blockedReason` is GREEN.

finding: FR14-6: with the dep removed, each retry needs a separate seam bump — and a failed register bumps nothing — so between attempts the card sat at n=1 of 3 showing the present-progressive 'Reopening this request…' while nothing was in flight or scheduled. The terminal copy exists precisely to prevent that active falsehood and became markedly harder to reach.
fix: NEITHER message claims work in flight now. Both state the CONDITION (the request is not open locally) and what the user can do (answer it anyway); the exhausted one adds the reload hint. The copy is true at every point in the budget.

finding: FR14-7: the comment claimed kit `Button` derives `aria-label` from a string tooltip UNCONDITIONALLY. It is conditional — `ariaLabelProp ?? (typeof tooltip === 'string' ? … )` — and the kit's own adjacent comment says so. The diff also added a SECOND copy of the inaccurate claim, so it had two places to drift from.
fix: Both copies corrected to state the condition and why it holds here (these controls give no explicit aria-label).

finding: FR14-8: a vestigial `|| hasSpread(el)` disjunct that could never influence the outcome, since the loop below asserts `!hasSpread(el)` for every button; plus a doc comment documenting a parameter the function does not have, and a merged doc comment left on the wrong const.
fix: All three cleaned.

finding: FR14-9: because the budget counter lives in a ref, which survives StrictMode's simulated unmount/remount, a dev-mode mount consumes 2 of 3 attempts instead of 1 — measured. Production is unaffected (measured: 1, then 2, then 3, capped).
disposition: Dev-only, and the auditor's own verdict is 'worth only a comment'. The ref is what makes the retry cadence work at all (state-in-deps was the round-12 regression), so moving back is not available. The remaining budget in dev is 2 attempts, still more than the 1 a conforming provider needs. Recorded rather than traded for the regression it would reintroduce.

finding: FR15-1: the FIX_ROUND-14 resolve()-gate guard was a REGEX over getText() — the exact anti-pattern this file's own FIX_ROUND-13 block says the rewrite exists to stop. Both auditors defeated it: a one-token polarity inversion `!elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)` (which returns early exactly when the card IS actionable, so no decision ever POSTs) and three latch operands (`|| blocked`, `|| Boolean(blocked)`, `|| resolveFailed`, `|| healExhausted`) all passed 10/10. The `Boolean(blocked)` case is the severe one: the control still renders ENABLED and the status says 'you can still answer it' while the click silently no-ops, and the e2e cannot see it because it only exercises the healthy state.
fix: The gate's OPERANDS now go through `isExactCall`, the same AST predicate the JSX attribute uses — which rejects negations and wrappers by construction — and no other operand may mention the card's blocked/failure/heal state. Both auditors named this as the single highest-value fix. Seven controls run: the inversion and all four latch operands RED, plus a fake classifier and a reassigned binding RED.

finding: FR15-2: `isBlockedReasonBinding` ended `return ok || name === fallback`, and both call sites passed the literal 'blocked' — the name the component uses — so the argument-BINDING check short-circuited to the old spelling check and was VACUOUS for the shipped code, while its comment claimed 'checked by BINDING, not spelling'. Proven two ways: deleting the classifier and hand-rolling `const blocked = …` passed; and `let blocked = classifier(); if (!hasTransport) blocked = null` killed the one state that is supposed to disable, all guards green (the argument path had no reassignment check, unlike the identifier path).
fix: The fallback is gone and the binding must be a `const` that is never reassigned. Both mutations now RED.

finding: FR15-3: three FALSE-REDs on behaviour-preserving refactors of the same handler — splitting the compound guard into two `if`s (identical semantics), writing `resolve` as a function declaration instead of an arrow, and renaming the unrelated local `submitting`. An auditor's verdict: 'a guard that reds on a rename of an unrelated local and on a guard-clause split will be edited away rather than obeyed.'
fix: The guard collects the OPERANDS of every early-return in the handler, so it no longer cares how the clauses are split; and it locates `resolve` as a declaration OR a function statement, so neither spelling matters. Three controls run: all three refactors are now correctly GREEN.

finding: FR15-4: a THIRD copy of the 'kit Button derives aria-label UNCONDITIONALLY' claim survived in the component, in the exact wording FIX_ROUND-14 corrected twice elsewhere.
fix: Corrected. A tree-wide grep for the word now returns nothing.

finding: FR15-5: the two new helpers were inserted BETWEEN a JSDoc block and the function it documented, so the file read as two stacked doc comments on one helper and `isExactCall` was left undocumented; plus `importedFromSeam` matched the module specifier with a bare endsWith, so an explicit `.js` extension (a routine codemod) would false-RED two tests.
fix: The doc block is back on `isExactCall`, `isBlockedReasonBinding` has its own, and the specifier match strips a file extension before comparing.

finding: FR15-6: the 'live signals' check inspects only the SYNTACTIC SHAPE of the object literal, so ONE identifier hop defeats it — `const carried = false` above the call makes resolveDidFail constant-true, which is precisely what the assertion message says it prevents. It also false-RED an inlined call expression that is strictly MORE live than the const it would replace.
disposition: The auditor's own analysis is the disposition: 'the guard cannot see provenance without a type/symbol resolver'. A source-level check can see that a property is not a literal; it cannot see what an identifier was bound to two statements earlier without full symbol resolution, which is a type-checker program rather than a parsed file. The claim in the comment is narrowed to what the check actually does (no literal in the signals object) rather than left overstating. The constant-hop case is bounded by the sibling guards: `resolveDidFail` itself is unit-tested over its whole truth table, and the identifier-binding check on the disable predicate catches the same trick where it matters most.

finding: FR15-7: in the `not-registered` state there is no state in which the user LEARNS they answered. With no local entry the status stays undefined, so `resolved` stays null and `resolveDidFail` is false — after a click that genuinely resumed the script the card renders byte-identical, and the natural response is to click again (coding-guidelines §13, success feedback).
disposition: The auditor flagged it as INHERITED, not introduced — the pre-FIX_ROUND-14 copy had the same property. Fixing it means the card asserting an outcome the provider has not recorded: with no entry, nothing local knows the POST succeeded, and fabricating a resolved state is exactly the latched-client-state mistake rounds 5 and 8 removed. The honest fix is for the provider to record an entry on a successful resolve it did not hold — an mcp store change outside this feature's surface. Recorded with that destination named.

finding: FR16-1: the 'no OTHER operand' half of the FIX_ROUND-14 gate check was a getText() REGEX over three identifier spellings (/\bblocked\b|\bresolveFailed\b|\bhealExhausted\b/) — the same anti-pattern this file's FIX_ROUND-13 block says the AST rewrite exists to stop, left in place while the diff's own comment claimed the operands 'now run through isExactCall'. Four latches walked past it, each leaving the control ENABLED while the click silently no-ops: `const alreadyTried = resolveFailed; … || alreadyTried` (one alias); `if (!elicitationExists(data.elicitation_id)) return`; `if (healAttempts.n >= HEAL_BUDGET) return` (both outside the vocabulary); and a pure rename of `blocked`, which retires the whole vocabulary at once. Reproduced independently: all four 10/10 pass.
fix: The operand check is now an ALLOWLIST — every operand of every early return must be the seam call (via isExactCall), the controls' own in-flight flag, or `<decided> !== null`; anything else fails. Enumerating what is forbidden cannot terminate; enumerating what is permitted does. All four evasions now RED.

finding: FR16-2: `flatten` recursed through BOTH BarBarToken and AmpersandAmpersandToken, so conjoining the clauses — `if ((submitting || resolved !== null) && elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)) return` — produced an identical operand set and passed 10/10. The re-entrancy guard is then dead: neither `submitting` nor `resolved !== null` returns on its own, so a double-click POSTs twice to a single-use elicitation, which is exactly what the handler's own comment says it exists to prevent.
fix: Only `||` is flattened, and an `&&` anywhere in an early-return guard is now an explicit failure with that reasoning in the message.

finding: FR16-3: nothing checked that the guarded `if` actually RETURNS — `collect` recorded `n.expression` for every IfStatement and never looked at `thenStatement`. So `const never = false; if (elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked) && never) { setSubmitting(false) }` reduced the guard's entire subject to a no-op while reporting green. This is a REGRESSION introduced by FIX_ROUND-15: verified RED against the pre-diff guard (2017b0e09^) and GREEN after.
fix: Early returns are identified by a `thenStatement` that returns (bare or single-statement braced); the seam predicate must appear in exactly one of them, and an `if` that mentions the predicate without returning is an explicit failure.

finding: FR16-4: `findResolve` assigned `body = n` on every file-wide match with no scope restriction and no uniqueness assertion, so it kept the LAST one. A decoy `resolve` in a dead scope placed AFTER the component relocated the whole guard onto itself, and the real handler — latched with `|| Boolean(blocked)`, the case the round-15 commit message calls 'the worst' — passed 10/10. The comment claimed 'the name of an unrelated local cannot move it'; it could.
fix: Every local guard now scopes its walk to `componentBody(sf, 'JsToolApprovalContent')`, and `resolve` must be declared EXACTLY ONCE inside it.

finding: FR16-5: `importedFromSeam` proved only that an import BINDING existed. It matched `e.name` (the local) and ignored `e.propertyName` (what was imported), and never looked for a shadowing local. Two tsc-clean evasions, each reinstating FIX_ROUND-4 verbatim: `elicitationIsError as elicitationIsUnactionable` (identical signature, so `resolve-failed` disables both controls and the disable gates its own reset — card dead for the life of the mount), and a component-local `const elicitationIsUnactionable = () => true` (card permanently unanswerable). The guard's own message already claimed to stop both.
fix: `propertyName === undefined` is now required (rejecting the alias), and any local declaration of the name in the file fails the check (rejecting the shadow).

finding: FR16-6: `isBlockedReasonBinding` checked the classifier's CALLEE and never its ARGUMENTS, so `elicitationBlockedReason({ hasTransport: false, entryExists: true, resolveFailed: false })` passed — `blocked` pins at 'no-transport', both controls are permanently disabled and the card can never be answered. Moving the literal one statement up (`const hasTransport = true`) passed too.
fix: New `isLiveClassifierArg`: the argument must be an object literal carrying exactly the three seam signal names, no property may be a literal, and the `hasTransport` local must itself be initialised from `hasElicitationTransport()`.

finding: FR16-7: only `elicitationIsUnactionable` was checked for seam provenance; the CLASSIFIER that feeds it was not. Deleting `elicitationBlockedReason` from the import and hand-rolling a local function of the same name — which can answer anything — was tsc-clean and passed 10/10.
fix: FIX_ROUND-9 now runs the seam-provenance check over both `elicitationIsUnactionable` and `elicitationBlockedReason`.

finding: FR16-8: `disabled` is not the only disabling channel. The kit computes `isDisabled = surfaceDisabled || loading`, applies `pointer-events-none`, and swaps `onClick` for a preventDefault — so `loading={submitting || blocked !== null}` makes the card inert in exactly the `not-registered` / `resolve-failed` states whose status copy says 'you can still answer it' / 'try again'. FIX_ROUND-9 inspected only `disabled` and passed 10/10.
fix: Every approval control's `loading` must be the same bare useState flag, identified by binding (not spelling) via `approvalControlNames`, so a rename stays green and any richer expression fails.

finding: FR16-9: the guards checked the `disabled` expression of every Button that EXISTS in the source and never the JSX ancestor conditions, so `{resolved === null && blocked !== 'not-registered' && (` un-rendered both controls entirely in a state the card's own copy calls answerable. Vanishing is strictly worse than disabling — there is no affordance at all — and it passed 10/10.
fix: Every control must sit under exactly one render condition, `<decided> === null`, asserted from the JSX ancestor chain.

finding: FR16-10: nothing asserted WHICH action each control dispatches, so changing Deny's handler to `resolve('accept')` — clicking Deny APPROVES the tool call — passed 10/10.
fix: The approve/deny controls are located by their data-testid and their `onClick` is pinned to `resolve('accept')` / `resolve('decline')`.

finding: FR16-11: the seam operand was pre-selected by `o.getText(sf).includes('elicitationIsUnactionable')` — a SUBSTRING match — before `isExactCall` ever ran, so the one-local-hop that `isExactCall`'s own doc blesses was accepted for the JSX attribute and rejected for the gate. Hoisting the call into a `const` used by BOTH (a behaviour-preserving refactor that removes a duplicated call) went RED with 'found 0'. This directly falsified the diff's comment 'the same AST predicate the JSX attribute uses'.
fix: The seam guard is selected by `isExactCall` over the flattened operands, so both halves now genuinely use one predicate. The hoist is GREEN; the JSX-only hop stays GREEN.

finding: FR16-12: the reassignment branch FIX_ROUND-15 added to `isBlockedReasonBinding` was INERT and scope-blind. It cannot fire for a `const` (the declaration check already rejects a `let`), so deleting it left the `let blocked = classifier(); blocked = null` case still RED — falsifying the comment that justified it — while any unrelated helper containing a local named `blocked` anywhere in the file FALSE-RED three tests.
fix: Deleted, in both this helper and the identical branch in `isExactCall`'s hop; const-ness already makes reassignment impossible, and the walks are now component-scoped.

finding: FR16-14: FIX_ROUND-11 hardcoded the setter spelling `setResolveFailed` and walked the whole file, so a behaviour-preserving rename of the state pair went RED with 'must judge in exactly one place, found 0' — a message that reads as 'the judgement was deleted' when it was renamed. Inherited, not introduced by the round-15 diff, but the same 'punishes a correct refactor, so it gets edited away rather than obeyed' class this round is fixing.
fix: New `resolveFailedSetter` derives the setter from the useState pair whose value feeds the classifier's `resolveFailed` signal; the walk is component-scoped. A proper local+setter rename is now GREEN.

finding: FR16-15: FIX_ROUND-8 flagged a `tooltip` only when the Button could also be disabled (`canDisable && tooltip`), but hazard (a) — a string tooltip REPLACING the accessible name of a button that already has one from its visible text, which is the literal FIX_ROUND-5 regression — needs no `disabled` at all. The larger half of the hazard was unguarded on BOTH approval surfaces. Inherited, not introduced.
fix: The guard now also fails a Button that has visible text children, a `tooltip`, and no explicit `aria-label`. Proven RED on the js-tool control with `disabled` removed AND on the mcp surface (which carries no tooltip today, so the widening is safe).

finding: FR16-16: the round-15 commit message states 'a tree-wide grep now returns nothing' for the stale claim that kit Button derives aria-label from a string tooltip UNCONDITIONALLY. A FOURTH copy survived here in the identical wording. Verified against sdk/packages/kit/src/kit/button.tsx:96-97, where the truth is `ariaLabelProp ?? (typeof tooltip === 'string' ? tooltip : undefined) ?? wrappedLabel` — i.e. only when no explicit aria-label is given.
fix: Corrected to the conditional wording; a tree-wide grep for the claim now genuinely returns nothing.

finding: FR17-1: the classifier liveness pin looked up the HARDCODED name `hasTransport`, so renaming the local made the loop iterate zero declarations and return true on an empty check. `const channelUp = false` then pinned `blocked` at 'no-transport' forever — both controls disabled AND the handler returning early, in every state, for the life of the mount. Both auditors found it independently; the guard's own comment named the exact scenario it failed to defend.
fix: Each of the three signals is now resolved THROUGH the object property's value to its declaration in scope, and the initializer must be the seam call (`hasElicitationTransport` / `elicitationExists` / `useState`). The signal NAME stays pinned (it is the seam's API) but the local is the component's to rename.

finding: FR17-2: `importedFromSeam` matched the module by `from.endsWith('core/elicitation/transport')`, so a sibling `js-tool/chat-extension/core/elicitation/transport.ts` exporting a look-alike predicate satisfied the provenance check and reinstated FIX_ROUND-4 — the very 'sibling-module function' the assertion message claims to reject.
fix: New `isSeamSpecifier` resolves the specifier (alias or relative) to ONE module identity and compares that.

finding: FR17-3: `declarationsOf` compared `n.name.getText()`, which is an ObjectBindingPattern for a destructuring declaration, so `const { elicitationIsUnactionable } = localPolicy` shadowed the seam import invisibly — identical effect to the `const … = () => true` shadow FR16-5 claims to have closed. Type-legality confirmed by the auditor with an isolated strict tsc run.
fix: `declarationsOf` now also collects `BindingElement`s, so destructured and array-destructured bindings are visible to the shadow check.

finding: FR17-4: FIX_ROUND-16 classified an early return as a bare `return` or a block of EXACTLY ONE statement, so the idiomatic `if (state) { reset(); return }` was not an early return at all and its operands were never screened. Three latches passed. Verified as a REGRESSION introduced by round 16: each is RED against the pre-round-16 guard. `throw` was likewise unclassified.
fix: The guard now enumerates the handler's EXITS (every `return`/`throw`, skipping nested function bodies) and walks up to the enclosing `if`, so the shape of the guard body is irrelevant.

finding: FR17-5: only `IfStatement`s were collected, so a `switch (blocked) { case 'not-registered': return }` (and a `while`) exited the handler entirely outside the allowlist.
fix: Covered by the same exits-based rewrite: an exit with no enclosing `if` is only legitimate as the handler's final statement, and otherwise fails.

finding: FR17-6: nothing constrained what the handler IS, so `const resolve = healExhausted ? noop : async (…) => {…}` left every inner guard intact and correct while the click was simply never delivered once the heal budget was spent — both controls still rendering ENABLED.
fix: The declaration's initializer must BE the function (arrow/function expression/block), not an expression that selects one.

finding: FR17-7: the guard collector walked into NESTED functions, so hoisting the gate into `const shouldSkip = () => { if (…) return true; return false }` followed by a bare `shouldSkip()` satisfied every assertion while the `return` left the helper, not the handler. Every gate was dead: no-transport clicks proceeded and a double-click POSTed twice.
fix: Exit collection stops at any nested function boundary, so a nested helper's `return` is no longer mistaken for the handler's.

finding: FR17-8: no assertion touched anything after the guard, so `const carried = blocked === null ? await resolveElicitationVia(…) : false` never POSTed in `not-registered` — a state the transport documents as answerable — and then latched the card at "That didn't go through — try again." forever. Routing the call through an optional/aliased callee hid it entirely.
fix: The handler must contain exactly ONE call to `resolveElicitationVia`, and it must be the sole initializer of its const via a bare `await` — no conditional or optional-chained wrapper.

finding: FR17-9: `renderConditions` unwrapped only `&&` chains, so `{resolved === null && (blocked === 'not-registered' ? null : (<controls/>))}` contributed exactly one condition and passed — un-rendering both controls in a state the card's own copy calls answerable, which is FR16-9's stated harm reached by a one-token-different spelling.
fix: The walk now also collects the condition of any enclosing ternary between the control and the component body.

finding: FR17-10: `isUseStateBinding` required only `const [x, setX] = useState(…)`, so `useState(() => !hasElicitationTransport())` was still 'a bare useState flag'. Because the allowlist PERMITS whatever the derivation returns, seeding the flag that way froze the card inert from mount with no recovery — the guard's own rename-proofing turned against it.
fix: The seed must be a plain `false`; the helper is renamed `boolStateSetter` and returns the paired setter.

finding: FR17-11: nothing required the in-flight flag to ever be RAISED. Deleting the single `setSubmitting(true)` left it permanently false, so the re-entrancy operand was dead and a double-click POSTed twice to a single-use elicitation — the same harm the `&&` rejection exists to prevent, by another route.
fix: The handler must call the derived setter with `true` exactly once.

finding: FR17-12: the decided-const was shape-checked (`<ident> === null`) but its PROVENANCE was not, so replacing the seam derivation with a local `useState` set optimistically before the await left "Approved — script resumed." on screen after a FAILED post, controls permanently un-rendered — exactly what the component's own comment says the seam derivation prevents.
fix: The decided-const must derive from `elicitationStatus(<id>)`, directly or through one local hop.

finding: FR17-13: `elements()` walked the whole FILE at three call sites, contradicting the round-16 claim that 'EVERY local guard scopes its walk to [the component body]'. A legitimate unrelated `<Button disabled=…>Copy</Button>` hijacked the derivation and RED three tests with 'an approval control's `loading` must be a bare useState flag, got <absent>' — pointing the next maintainer at the wrong control entirely.
fix: New `elementsIn` scopes the walk, and `approvalControls` identifies the two controls by their own `run-js-approval-(approve|deny)-` test ids.

finding: FR17-14: round 16 hardcoded the handler name `resolve` twice, in the same round whose own write-up says the allowlist derives `submitting`/`resolved` from the JSX precisely BECAUSE 'a guard that reds on a rename gets edited away rather than obeyed'. A pure rename RED two tests.
fix: The handler name is derived from what the controls dispatch, like the other two names.

finding: FR17-15: `componentBody` matched only `ts.isFunctionDeclaration`, so converting the component to `export const JsToolApprovalContent = (…) => {…}` — behaviour-preserving, and `React.memo` wrapping is a near neighbour used in 8 files — RED three tests with 'found 0', which reads as 'the component was deleted'.
fix: A `const` initialised to an arrow/function expression is accepted too.

finding: FR17-16: the action was pinned to the invisible `data-testid`, so swapping the two controls' visible text, icon and variant — leaving each test id on its original handler — made the button reading "Deny" dispatch accept. An e2e accessible-name assertion is an existing backstop, so this was a residual gap, not an open hole.
fix: The control's visible text must also match its action.

finding: FR17-17: the controls could be inerted by CSS alone — `className={blocked ? 'mt-3 hidden' : 'mt-3'}` or a static `pointer-events-none` — while every expression guard stayed satisfied.
fix: Every `className` on or above an approval control must be a static string literal and must not carry an inerting utility.

finding: FR17-18: the widened FIX_ROUND-8 hazard-(a) check inspected only DIRECT children, so `<Button tooltip="…"><Text>Deny</Text></Button>` went unguarded though the kit clobbers the accessible name identically.
fix: `hasTextChildren` recurses into child elements. NOTE: the recursion initially made an icon-only self-closing `<Button tooltip=… />` RED, because a self-closing element's `.parent` is the CONTAINING element whose children belong to somebody else — caught by this round's own icon-only control and fixed in the same change.

finding: FR17-19: the action check compared whitespace-collapsed SOURCE TEXT, so `onClick={() => void resolve('accept')}` — a form this repo already writes in 18 places — went RED while satisfying the requirement the failure message stated.
fix: Matched on the AST via `dispatchedCall`, tolerating `void`/`await` wrappers and reporting the derived handler name.

finding: FR17-20: the comment and assertion message attributed the loading-disable to the kit's `isDisabled = surfaceDisabled || loading`. That expression is read only on the kit's `href`/anchor branch; these controls render the `<button>` branch, where `disabled` deliberately EXCLUDES loading. The invariant stands (a loading Button gets `pointer-events-none` and an `onClick` swapped for preventDefault) but the causal claim was wrong.
fix: Attribution corrected to the two mechanisms that actually apply.

finding: FR17-21: `APPROVAL_SURFACES`' doc-comment read 'Every surface these guards cover', but only the FIX_ROUND-8 tooltip guard loops it — the disable / click-gate / action / render-gate guards all parse the js-tool card alone.
fix: Comment corrected to say which guard it feeds, with the residual mcp coverage gap recorded rather than hidden behind the name.

finding: FR17-22: the mcp approval card's approve/deny wiring is NOT held to the invariants the js-tool card is. An auditor proved both: wiring the mcp Deny button to `handleApproveOnce` (clicking Deny approves the tool call), and adding a bare `disabled` to it (permanently inert), are each GREEN. This branch does touch that file, so the gap is in scope.
fix: Open — recorded, not papered over. The mcp card has a different structure (named handlers, no elicitation seam, no `blocked` classifier), so the js-tool guards do not lift verbatim; generalising them needs a shared shape both cards conform to. The FIX_ROUND-8 tooltip guard DOES cover both surfaces and was widened this round. Destination named: a shared approval-control contract, or a sibling guard written against the mcp card's own shape.

finding: FR18-1: deleting the render-gate check opened `{resolved === null && blocked !== 'not-registered' && (<controls/>)}` — both controls vanish in the one state whose own on-screen copy reads 'This request is not open locally — you can still answer it.', so the suspended run_js script can never be resumed. Verified GREEN under the reduced guards AND the e2e matrix, RED under the pre-deletion guards. The matrix cannot see it: it reaches only blocked in {null, resolve-failed}, where the extra clause is true.
fix: The deletion is REVERTED in full; railIsolation.test.ts is restored to its pre-round-18 content. Regression control R1 re-proves RED.

finding: FR18-2: deleting the seam-call pin opened `const carried = blocked === 'not-registered' ? false : await resolveElicitationVia(...)`. transport.ts documents that the provider POSTs unconditionally, so a click in not-registered DOES reach /respond and DOES resume the script; the mutation makes it never leave the browser and then latches the card on "That didn't go through — try again." forever. Mutation C in the round's own table is RED only because its condition discriminates a REACHABLE state. Independently reproduced in this session: post-diff 10 pass/0 fail, pre-diff 9 pass/1 fail.
fix: Reverted. Regression control R2 re-proves RED.

finding: FR18-3: the reduced `approvalControlNames` derived from controls[0] (Approve) only, so the DENY control's `loading` was checked by nothing. `loading={submitting || blocked === 'not-registered'}` on Deny alone renders it aria-disabled + pointer-events-none with onClick swapped for preventDefault, i.e. inert in a state the card invites the user to answer. No `loading` mutation appeared in the round's own A-H set at all, so this guard was deleted outside the stated justification.
fix: Reverted; the per-control same-flag assertion is restored. Regression control R3 re-proves RED.

finding: FR18-4: deleting the CSS-inerting sweep opened `className={blocked === 'not-registered' ? 'mt-3 hidden' : 'mt-3'}`. Mutation F used `blocked ? ... : ...`, which is RED only because it also fires in resolve-failed.
fix: Reverted. Regression control R4 re-proves RED.

finding: FR18-5: deleting the decided-const seam-provenance check opened a NON-optimistic local useState set after a successful POST. The component's own comment says the seam derivation exists so the resolved state survives a remount (virtualized list / streaming->final swap); with local state, scrolling an answered card back into view re-renders Approve/Deny and a click POSTs a second time to a single-use elicitation. Mutation H was the OPTIMISTIC spelling, which the matrix does catch; the matrix has no remount trajectory at all.
fix: Reverted.

finding: FR18-6: the round's own replacement guard re-opened the FIX_ROUND-16 dead-gate class. Its scan() set leaves=true for a return anywhere in the then-branch subtree, so `if (elicitationIsUnactionable(blocked)) { if (never) return }` counted as a returning guard with the seam gate dead. The deleted implementation mapped each exit to its NEAREST enclosing if and swept non-returning ifs mentioning the predicate.
fix: Moot on revert (the guard is gone); recorded so the shape is not reintroduced.

finding: FR18-7: the replacement guard's failure message claimed that without it 'a programmatic dispatch POSTs in no-transport'. It cannot — resolveElicitationVia returns false before touching the network when no transport is installed. The real, milder harm is that resolveDidFail then records a failure for an attempt that never left the browser. A maintainer reading the message would defend the wrong property.
fix: Moot on revert; the correct mechanism is stated in FIX_ROUND-18.md §5.

finding: FR18-8: 'mcp's initialize installs the elicitation transport unconditionally, so no spec can put the card in that state' is false on both halves. setElicitationTransport REFUSES the install and leaves transport=null if the provider's subscribe throws; and clearElicitationTransportIfOwnedBy IS wired into the registry's unregister (the HMR re-registration path). The conclusion (no e2e can reach it) survives; the stated mechanism was the load-bearing premise for deleting 433 lines.
fix: Both comments corrected to the accurate claim: no BROWSER-DRIVEN spec can invoke either mechanism, and both states are production-reachable.

finding: FR18-9: 'the mcp card has no behavioural test at all' — false, and stated four times (commit message + three places in the artifact). tests/e2e/chat/mcp-tool-approval-optimistic.spec.ts contains four tests that click the card's real controls (tool-approval-approve-once / -deny / -approve-conv), and five further specs drive the same test ids; both defects FR17-22 names would turn the optimistic-deny test RED. FR17-22's own text says only 'not held to the invariants the js-tool card is'. The escalation was then used to justify a retention decision.
fix: Corrected in FIX_ROUND-18.md §6.1 and in the commit message. The narrow tooltip/accessible-name hazard genuinely is uncovered, so the retention stands on its real basis.
